'exact': minimize w_amips * AMIPS + (1-w_amips) * (d/eps)^2 with the true region-wise Hessian of the distance to the piecewise-linear input; sliding is free where the input is flat, held at corners, constrained along 3D edges and curve segments. Rests a w_amips-proportional distance off the input.

docs.title: w_amips
docs.text:
float · default 0.0001

Relative weight of the AMIPS quality term against the envelope term during smoothing; the envelope weight is 1 - w_amips. The small default makes smoothing primarily about staying on the surface, with quality as a secondary preference.

docs.title: num_smoothing_passes
docs.text:
int · default 2

Number of smoothing passes per optimization iteration. Smoothing is the only phase that improves quality without changing connectivity, so when split, collapse and swap have run out of useful moves it is the only thing that can still lower the energy. Was 10; lowered to 2 once surface vertices stopped being skipped by skip_good_regions, which made each pass do real work -- on Thingi10K 240280 a pass costs 41-51s and moves fewer vertices each time (accepted 18606 -> 17077 over five passes, envelope rejections 11316 -> 12237), so the later passes in a run of 10 buy very little for their cost.

docs.title: interleaved_smoothing
docs.text:
bool · default true

Interleave smoothing between the topology passes: split + smoothing, collapse + smoothing, swaps + smoothing, instead of split, collapse, swaps followed by num_smoothing_passes smoothing passes. On by default in both applications: each topology pass then sees a relaxed mesh rather than the raw output of the previous one. Measured in 2D on 122839, where per iteration it reached a given energy sooner than the batched schedule (102 vs 535 at iteration 5, 25 vs 69 at iteration 13), at roughly 3x the work per iteration since each topology pass gets its own smoothing.

docs.title: interleaved_smoothing_passes
docs.text:
int · default 1

Smoothing passes to run after each topology pass when interleaved_smoothing is set. One is enough with interleaving on, since there are three of them per iteration.

docs.title: check_surface_folds
docs.text:
bool · default false

Refuse a collapse, swap or smoothing that folds the tracked surface over: one that leaves more tracked faces facing against, or flat to, the surface it replaces (the tracked faces around it, their area vectors summed) or the surface it leaves than there were, or more such faces in the stars of the surface vertices it touches. Exact (orient3d). A fold the input has can be undone, but none is made. Splits are not checked: they move no vertex. Turns colored_smoothing off.

docs.title: colored_smoothing
docs.text:
bool · default true

Parallel smoothing (num_threads > 0) by color class: the vertices are split into classes of pairwise non-adjacent vertices, smoothed one class after another, each class fully in parallel without locks. The result does not depend on the number of threads. false: the locked, partitioned smoothing pass, whose result depends on the thread schedule. Serial runs (num_threads 0) are the same either way.

docs.title: remove_duplicate_eps
docs.text:
float · default 0

Remove duplicate vertices in the input meshes that are closer than this fraction of the bounding box diagonal. This is applied to each input mesh separately. 0 merges only exactly coincident vertices, which is still needed to build the surface connectivity; negative skips the pass entirely. Ignored when preserve_topology is set: merging vertices that are merely close welds sheets of the surface together and so removes handles, therefore only exactly coincident vertices are merged in that case.

docs.title: allow_surface_swap
docs.text:
bool · default true

Allow the edge swaps (3-2, 4-4, 5-6) to operate on surface edges, as a topology-preserving surface diagonal flip. When false, every surface edge is left alone.

docs.title: check_surface_topology
docs.text:
bool · default false

Check if the surface topology is preserved after each operation. This can be very slow and should only be used for debugging.

docs.title: volume_history_output
docs.text:
string · default ""

With history_output. Also record the tets around every operation that changes the tracked surface, and save them here (see wmtk/history/VolumeHistory.hpp): with the surface history, the tracking component rebuilds a map of the whole volume -- one region, the tracked surface kept on itself -- from the tet mesh the optimization starts from, written as <output>_history_input.msh, to the mesh before the filter, written as <output>_history_output.msh. On the memory route no file is written: any non-empty value records the volume history, the bytes of the file it would be are returned in the report as volume_history (bytes in Python; history::write_history or wm.write_history saves them), and the two meshes as the output meshes history_input and history_output, the rows of the files. It takes several times the room of the surface history. Not with use_legacy_code, nor with coarsen_pass and coarsen_local_smoothing_passes above 0: the coarsening composite smooths a ball of vertices inside one collapse, which the volume history does not see. Empty: no recording.

docs.title: max_expected_iterations
docs.text:
int · default 0

Fail the run if mesh_improvement needed more than this many iterations, even if it did reach stop_energy. 0 disables the check. This is a regression guard rather than a quality target: an input that normally converges in a handful of iterations and suddenly needs the whole budget means the sizing-refinement trigger stopped firing when it should, which is a silent slowdown that no energy or envelope assertion catches.

docs.title: stuck_refine_stall_eps
docs.text:
float · default 0.1

Refine when the last iteration's improvement was at most this fraction of the distance the max energy still has to cover: (prev_max - max) <= eps * (max - stop_energy). Equivalently, refine unless the mesh is on course to reach the target within about 1/eps more iterations. 0 => only when it does not improve at all.

docs.title: stuck_refine_cooldown
docs.text:
int · default 1

After a refinement, skip this many improvement iterations before refining again (let the operations act on the new sizing field). 1 by default: refining every iteration can outrun the operations entirely -- on triwild20k 189017 at eps_rel 1e-4 the mesh runs away to 5.8M faces and never converges at 0, and converges at 9.9994 in 35 iterations at 1. Costs ~5% iterations across the challenging models at no wall-time cost.

docs.title: stuck_refine_num_worst
docs.text:
int · default 0 · min 0

Number of worst tets whose neighborhoods are refined when stuck. 0 => refine all tets with energy above the filter_energy.

docs.title: stuck_refine_rings
docs.text:
int · default 0 · min 0

Graph rings around each worst tet included in the stuck refinement. 0 => only the worst tet itself, 1 => its neighbors, 2 => neighbors of neighbors, etc.

docs.title: stuck_refine_factor
docs.text:
float · default 0.5

Multiplicative reduction of the sizing scalar per stuck refinement (0.5 => halve).

docs.title: stuck_refine_min_scalar
docs.text:
float · default 0.001

Lower bound on the sizing scalar during stuck refinement.

docs.title: stuck_refine_gradation
docs.text:
float · default 2.0

Gradation cap for the monotone sizing smoothing: adjacent sizings may differ by at most this factor (smoothing only lowers values).

docs.title: stuck_refine_force_split
docs.text:
bool · default true

When the max energy stalls, split each worst tet's longest edge once, bypassing the split length gate, to unstick a sliver without changing the sizing field. Adds at most one split per worst tet per stall.

docs.title: skip_good_regions
docs.text:
bool · default false

Only smooth vertices incident to a tet whose energy is at least skip_good_regions_margin * stop_energy; skip smoothing already-good regions. OFF by default: smoothing is the only phase that improves quality without changing connectivity, and the premise that a vertex surrounded by good elements has nothing to gain is not reliable -- for surface vertices the move is driven by the envelope term rather than by element quality, which is why active_vertices() has to append every surface vertex unconditionally to keep the filter from freezing them outright. With the filter off that special case stops carrying the correctness of the pass. Measured in 2D on 122839 at stop_energy 20, filtering also cost more than it saved: 60 iterations ending at max energy 21.03 with it on, against convergence to 19.9998 in 54 iterations and less wall time (875s vs 947s) with it off. Note the threshold scales with stop_energy, so the filter skips far more at 100 than at 20.

docs.title: skip_good_regions_margin
docs.text:
float · default 0.9

A tet is 'active' (worth smoothing around) when its energy is at least this fraction of stop_energy.

docs.title: coarsen_local_smoothing_passes
docs.text:
int · default 0

Smoothing sweeps over the ring, inside each candidate collapse, before judging it. 0 by default, which means the pass judges the collapse on its raw post-collapse geometry and never smooths inside the operation. At the level of a single candidate that matters -- the composite's reject rate rises from 25% to 39% without it -- but it does not cost coarsening, because the pass runs to a fixed point: a candidate the smoothing would have rescued is replaced by another the pass finds instead, and the relaxation the mesh actually needs comes from the global smoothing between rounds. What it costs is time. The smoothed ball averaged 98 vertices on tetwild's octocat, so at the old default of 2 sweeps one candidate ran ~200 nonlinear smoothing solves and the pass ran 1.4 million of them to accept 5173 collapses. Over seven tetwild models, dropping this to 0 (with coarsen_max_inner_passes 1) made the pass 9.7x to 31.9x faster for about 1 percentage point of cell reduction.

docs.title: coarsen_smooth_ring
docs.text:
int · default 1

Radius smoothed inside the collapse, and the radius the accept test measures over. The lock claims one more ring than this. With coarsen_local_smoothing_passes at 0 nothing is smoothed, so this only sets how wide a region the accept test compares; a wider region is a more permissive test (it admits untouched cells to both the before and after maxima, which is still sound) so ring 2 coarsens slightly more, but it also makes the pass lock 3 rings per operation where the ordinary collapse locks 2, which is the worst thing for its parallel scaling. 1 by default: on octocat that is 2.3x faster than ring 2 for 1.5 percentage points of cell reduction, and it puts the lock footprint back in line with every other pass.

docs.title: coarsen_global_smoothing_passes
docs.text:
int · default 1

Ordinary whole-mesh smoothing passes run between coarsening rounds. This is what makes a second round worth running at all -- see coarsen_max_rounds -- so setting it to 0 collapses the rounds to one.

docs.title: coarsen_max_rounds
docs.text:
int · default 2

Cap on the coarsen/smooth alternation; the pass also stops as soon as a round accepts no collapse. A round does NOT exist to finish what the previous one started: within a round the collapse pass already runs to a fixed point, so repeating the collapse alone finds nothing. What a round adds is the global smoothing in between, which moves that fixed point -- the dirty-epoch retry only re-offers failures next to a SUCCESSFUL collapse, so a whole-mesh smoothing pass is invisible to it, and a rejected composite is rolled back in full so rejections never accumulate progress within a round. Returns decay fast: measured over the 16 challenging triwild models at five rounds, accepted collapses by round were 68.8% / 21.7% / 7.2% / 1.8% / 0.5%. Every round costs a full pre-check sweep over all edges plus a smoothing pass, so the default is two -- they carry 90.5% of the coarsening, and the three that would follow are worth 9.5% for 60% of the pass's budget.

docs.title: coarsen_max_inner_passes
docs.text:
int · default 1

Cap on the collapse pass's own dirty-epoch retry loop within one coarsening round; 0 is uncapped. Distinct from coarsen_max_rounds, which counts collapse+global-smoothing alternations. This counts the passes the retry loop makes inside a single collapse pass, re-offering failures whose neighbourhood a successful collapse disturbed. That filter asks only whether the neighbourhood MOVED, not whether it moved helpfully, so a productive first pass re-offers most of the mesh. 1 by default, i.e. one pass per round and no retry within it: on octocat the first pass found 5110 collapses in 135.8s and the three that followed found 27 in 38.4s. Rounds still repeat the pass, and those do pay off, because the global smoothing between them moves the fixed point in a way this filter cannot see.

docs.title: coarsen_unbounded
docs.text:
bool · default true

Coarsen as far as the quality guarantee allows, instead of stopping at the target edge length. The pass answers 'how few elements can hold this max energy', and that is a more aggressive question than it sounds -- the answer ignores how big the elements become. Measured on the registered tetwild models it takes them from 348k to 60k cells (-82.7%) at max energy raised on none of them, against -43.2% with this off, because a converged mesh is sized by length_rel and the adaptive sizing field rather than by what the quality target strictly requires. On by default: the element count is the thing worth having. Turned off, the pass leaves alone any edge already at or past the collapse threshold (0.8 * the target length, the same one the ordinary collapse uses), since collapsing it only makes its neighbours longer still. The sizing FIELD is deliberately not applied either way: that is the optimizer's own refinement scratch work, and honouring it here would leave the pass unable to undo refinement that turned out to be unnecessary.

docs.title: input_dir
docs.text:
string · default ""

Directory where the input files are located. This is injected by the application and should not be set by the user.

docs.title: num_threads
docs.text:
int · default 0

Number of threads. 0 runs sequentially and gives the same result on every run; with more threads the order of the operations depends on the schedule, and the result can change slightly from run to run.

docs.title: log_file
docs.text:
string · default ""

Logs are not just printed on the terminal but also saved in this file.

docs.title: report
docs.text:
string · default ""

A JSON file that stores information about the result and the method execution, e.g., runtime.

docs.title: throw_on_fail
docs.text:
bool · default false

Throw exception if the output does not fulfil the desired criteria. No output will be generated.

docs.title: Debug options
docs.text:
Diagnostics: slow checks and extra output files. (6)

DEBUG_feature_retention · bool · default false

Sanity check: count how many feature anchors still have a mesh vertex within the anchor ball, measured BEFORE any /filter discards regions (a feature preserved through the optimization is never reported lost because extraction dropped its region; the feature outputs keep it either way), and report the worst miss in multiples of the ball radius. The invariant preserve_feature_points maintains, measured rather than assumed.

DEBUG_output · bool · default false

Write the mesh as debug_{}.vtu after every operation.

DEBUG_sanity_checks · bool · default false

Perform sanity checks after every operation. This can be very slow and should only be used for debugging.

DEBUG_hausdorff · bool · default false

Sanity Check: Compute and report the Hausdorff distance of the output to the input. Should be always smaller than eps.

DEBUG_euler · bool · default false

Sanity Check: Compute and report the Euler characteristic of the input and output surfaces and warn if they differ. Off by default because on meshes with many components it can take tens of seconds. It is computed regardless when preserve_topology is set (the topology check needs it).

DEBUG_disable_envelope · bool · default false

Diagnostic only. Disables every envelope containment check during the tetrahedralisation, after the input simplification has run. The envelope is the only thing that rejects an operation for geometric rather than combinatorial reasons, so this answers whether a stalled optimization is blocked by the envelope or by the mesh. The output has no containment guarantee and must not be used.

docs.title: Topological offset (topological_offset)
docs.text:
Adds a region at a target distance around a selection of a tagged tet mesh (the 2D offset, on triangle meshes, is refused for now): the boundary of a tag, an expression of tags, or an open curve or sheet. It grows the offset band from the selection and optimizes the mesh until the band's front lies at the target distance, keeping the band's topology throughout.

Tutorial · Spec source · Defaults · JSON Schema

Cite: Topological Offsets, ACM TOG 2025

docs.title: application
docs.text:
string · required · one of topological_offset

Application name must be topological_offset.

docs.title: input
docs.text:
string · required

Input mesh, .msh: a tetrahedral mesh (a triangle mesh is refused for now: the 2D offset is being brought up to date). The two pipelines are the same algorithm one dimension apart and read every key below the same way.

docs.title: output
docs.text:
string · default "out"

Output file name (without extension).

docs.title: offset_selection
docs.text:
string · default "!_"

Boolean expression for input simplicial complex to offset. If a single tag (ie 'tag_0') is given, single body mode is used.

docs.title: offset_output_tags
docs.text:
list of string · default ["newtag"]

Tags to add to elements in the resulting offset region.

Each entry: A tag.

docs.title: protected_tags
docs.text:
list of string · default []

Set of tags that will not be overwritten by the offset.

Each entry: A tag.

docs.title: offset_in
docs.text:
bool · default false

Only relevant for single body mode. Whether to create offset inside body

docs.title: offset_out
docs.text:
bool · default true

Only relevant for single body mode. Whether to create offset outside body

docs.title: target_distance_rel
docs.text:
float · default 0.01

Target offset distance relative to the bounding box diagonal of the mesh. Ignored if target_distance > 0.

docs.title: target_distance
docs.text:
float · default -1.0

Target distance for offset. If <= 0 (the default -1): derived from target_distance_rel.

docs.title: front_conv_rel
docs.text:
float · default 0.025

THE convergence epsilon as a fraction of target_distance, used when front_conv is <= 0; ignored if front_conv > 0. Since 2026-10-21: the config's target_distance, fixed for the whole run -- every growth_mode stage and attempt included, though they run at smaller target. Must not exceed 1 (startup refuses front_conv above target_distance). 0.025 (the default): a fully default run keeps the bar it had, 2.5e-4 x the bounding box diagonal at the default target_distance_rel 0.01. From 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-20 this key was a fraction of the bounding box diagonal (default 2.5e-4): a value written for that meaning now asks for a bar target_distance / diagonal times as large (1/100 at the default target). See front_conv for what the bar gates.

docs.title: optimize_offset
docs.text:
bool · default true

Run the optimization (optimize_offset: pre-loop setup, the loop's turns, the final pass and the convergence verdict) after the offset is constructed. Default true. false: the run stops at the constructed offset -- the simplicial embedding, the marching and the tag assignment still run -- and writes it as the result. The constructed band lies on the background mesh's own cell boundaries, so its distance to the input complex is set by the input mesh's resolution, not by target_distance; the report then carries only the before/after counts, threads and time -- no converged, offset_level, offset_dhat or optimization_metrics -- and throw_on_nonconvergence is not consulted. The offset potential is built only for the optimization, so with false phi_grid_resolution is ignored (with a warning) and the save_vtu file's energy and distance fields are NaN.

docs.title: max_rounds
docs.text:
int · default 40

The outer loop's budget, in turns, one turn being split, collapse and swap with smoothing after each, followed by the front test. An upper bound rather than a schedule -- exhausting it is a warning and not an error, because a front that needs more turns is a legitimate outcome to inspect.

docs.title: num_threads
docs.text:
int · default 0

Number of threads used for parallel execution (smoothing, edge collapse). 0 means single-threaded.

docs.title: check_manifoldness
docs.text:
bool · default true

After performing offset, check if offset region is manifold

docs.title: throw_on_nonconvergence
docs.text:
bool · default false

If true, a run that finishes without meeting the convergence criteria raises an error instead of logging a warning. Default false: a non-converged offset is still a usable one, and the warnings already name which criterion failed. Integration tests set it true so a convergence regression fails the run rather than passing with a warning.

docs.title: envelope_size_rel
docs.text:
float · default 0.001

Half-width, relative to the bounding box diagonal, of the envelope that holds the held surfaces during optimization; any operation that would push a held face outside it is rejected, and a held vertex is smoothed toward it. 3D: ONE envelope around every held face, built after the simplicial embedding, before the repulsion and the march: during the loop the domain wall and the input complex's boundary; in a TetWild pass (the final pass, and optimize_construction's) every other region boundary as well, at its position then (see use_rest_pose). The offset surface is never in it, but in a TetWild pass it is held to an envelope of its own with this same eps (since 2026-10-20, when offset_envelope / offset_envelope_rel were removed; optimize_construction's pass holds it to half the traced distance instead). This eps is also the derived sizing floor when min_edge_length_rel is negative. 2D: one envelope per region tag, as before. Ignored if envelope_size > 0.

docs.title: envelope_size
docs.text:
float · default -1.0

Absolute half-width of the envelope that holds the held surfaces (see envelope_size_rel). If <= 0 (the default -1): derived from envelope_size_rel.

docs.title: offset_field
docs.text:
string · default "euclidean" · one of smooth, euclidean

Which field defines the offset, and so what the front is placed on, what the criterion measures and what the sizing field refines by. 'smooth' is the offset geometric contact potential Phi, with the front on the level set Phi = c: C^2, analytic derivatives, and a level set that bulges outward at reentrant features, so it is a smoothed offset rather than the exact one. 'euclidean' (the default) is the exact distance to the input complex, which makes the residual exact but introduces a gradient discontinuity across the medial axis and a crease at every reentrant feature that no refinement resolves; offset_dhat_factor and the outside-the-support guard stop meaning anything, since it has no compact support. 3D refuses 'smooth' with an error at startup: the 3D energy's band term reads the euclidean distance, and the smooth field has no band term; 'smooth' is 2D only.

docs.title: offset_dhat_factor
docs.text:
float · default 2.0

Support radius of the smooth offset potential, as a multiple of target_distance. Must be > 1. The offset level set lies strictly inside the support; a band vertex that leaves the support is a hard error.

docs.title: front_conv
docs.text:
float · default -1.0

THE convergence epsilon, as an ABSOLUTE length in model units; <= 0 (the default -1): derived from front_conv_rel. Absolute or relative: front_conv_rel is a fraction of target_distance (since 2026-10-21; of the bounding box diagonal from 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-20). Startup refuses a value above target_distance: an epsilon coarser than the offset it measures decides nothing, since every front face then reads as resolved from the first turn. THIS IS THE ONLY BAR, in 2D and 3D. The measure it gates is one quantity everywhere: over a face's stencil_order stencil (in 2D a front chord's), the ROOT MEAN SQUARE of the distance to the level set along the field, over target_distance (for 'euclidean' the relative error (Phi - c)/c = (d - target_distance)/target_distance; for 'smooth' the root of Phi = c along grad Phi, since there (Phi - c)/c is not a length and read 3.44x the distance error at offset_dhat_factor 2), taken as a length. A face is resolved when that RMS is <= front_conv, i.e. when the MEAN SQUARED relative error is <= (front_conv/target_distance)^2; a vertex is placed when the same measure at the vertex alone -- the order-0 stencil -- is within it. So the vertex measure and the face measure are ONE measure at two sample counts, which is why vertex_conv and sag_conv, which split them apart on 2026-09-23, no longer exist. The offset surface debug field f_err reports the same number. The 2D front smoothing objective (StencilEnergy2D) has the same zero set but, under 'smooth', charges the field error (Phi - c)/c rather than this distance: about 3.44x it at offset_dhat_factor 2. The 3D smoothing objective is the energy (see offset_amips_weight), which has no face term. WHAT THE LOOP EXITS ON is set by front_measure: under the default 'vertex_ring', every front vertex's ring measure (the RMS of its offset faces' measures, every face weighted equally) within the bar; under 'face', the rule of 2026-09-25, every offset face's measure within the bar. Either way nothing may be unmeasurable, the single-point vertex measure is a diagnostic that decides nothing about termination, and an element over the bar that refinement cannot take (the sizing floor) blocks the exit and is named in a warning every turn it exists. 2D runs the same criterion on its front chords (offset edges in place of offset faces).

docs.title: stencil_order
docs.text:
int · default 1 · min 0

3D: the lattice below is EXPERIMENTAL_stencil_type "subdivision", the default; "interior" and "fem" (2026-10-27 / 28) have their own lattices for the same order k and need k >= 1 (see there). Order of the sampling stencil on an offset-surface face (3D) or front chord (2D). It sets the convergence measure, and in 2D also the front smoothing energy, which samples the same points; the 3D energy has no face term (see offset_amips_weight). Order 0 is the 3 CORNERS alone, so the measure is exactly the three vertices' own placement error. Order k >= 1 is the vertices of the triangle subdivided k-1 times by 4-way midpoint refinement, plus the centroid of each of its 4^(k-1) sub-triangles: with n = 2^(k-1) segments per side that is (n+1)(n+2)/2 + n^2 points, i.e. 4 at order 1 (the corners and the centroid), 10 at order 2 (the corners, the 3 edge midpoints and the 4 sub-triangle centroids), 31 at order 3, 109 at order 4. On a 2D chord the same rule one dimension down: order 0 is the 2 ENDS alone, order k >= 1 the vertices of the chord cut into 2^(k-1) pieces plus the midpoint of each piece, i.e. 3, 5, 9, 17 points. THE CORNERS ARE IN THE STENCIL, unlike the strictly interior lattice sag_num_samples used, and they have to be: the quantity sampled is a distance to the level set, which at a corner is that vertex's own placement error rather than the identically-zero interpolation error the old measure saw there. That is what lets one stencil replace the separate vertex and sag criteria. COST: every sample is a Phi value, paid in the criterion and the frames, and in 2D also in the operations' energy rules (TopoOffsetTriMesh::tri_energy()) and, with a gradient, in every front solve -- 4 points at the default against 6 for the old default.

docs.title: front_measure
docs.text:
string · default "vertex_ring" · one of vertex_ring, face

Which measure the loop exits on and refines by, in 3D and in 2D. 'vertex_ring' (the default): at each front vertex v the RING MEASURE r_v = sqrt((1/n_v) sum_f m_f^2), over the n_v offset faces f incident to v whose three corners are front vertices, every face weighted equally, m_f the face measure, the root of face_offset_term() (the RMS over the face's stencil_order stencil of the distance to the level set along the field over target_distance -- for 'euclidean' the relative error (Phi - c)/c -- over the bar front_conv / target_distance). The loop exits when every ring measure is within the bar and nothing is unmeasurable; a vertex with an unmeasurable incident face has no ring measure and blocks the exit. The face and vertex measures are then reported as diagnostics. The halving lowers the sizing scalar at each vertex whose ring measure is over the bar, that vertex alone, under the same floor (max of min_sizing_scalar and min_edge_length / l); a vertex over the bar already at the floor blocks the exit and is named by the [sizing floor] warning. The chord rule is not read in this mode. The operations do not compare this measure (until 2026-09-28 an ops guard compared the ring measure before against after): in 3D the collapse, the swaps and the smoother compare the energy (TopoOffsetTetMesh::tet_energy(), see offset_amips_weight), whose band term is a volume integral of the distance error, not these face measures. From 2026-09-25 to 2026-09-28 this measure weighted each face by its area (A_f); it weights every face equally since. In 2D the same criterion runs on the front chords: r_v = sqrt((1/n_v) sum_e m_e^2) over the n_v front chords e incident to v, m_e the chord measure (the root of edge_offset_term()), every chord weighted equally, with the same exit and the same per-vertex halving; 2D's operations compare the per-cell energy TopoOffsetTriMesh::tri_energy() and its front smoother minimises StencilEnergy2D, the same chords' m_e^2. 'face': the rule of 2026-09-25, kept for comparison. The loop exits when every offset face's (2D: chord's) measure is within the bar and nothing is unmeasurable; the halving lowers the sizing scalar at the corners of every face over the bar whose chord rule still has a target below its corners' scalars. Why the ring measure: the smoother minimises a sum over each vertex's ring while the face exit and refinement are per face, and the two disagree at the margin. Measured on the deliverable cube at target_distance_rel 1e-3 / front_conv_rel 1e-5 under 'face', turns 12-15: the loop never exits because a handful of faces end each turn at 1.00 to 1.19 times the bar, the smoothing having pushed faces from 0.99 to just over the bar while lowering the ring they belong to. On the cube at target_distance_rel 1e-2 / front_conv_rel 1e-4 (the split gate at twice the collapse gate, a key since removed, interleaved_smoothing false, 2 smoothing passes, no alignment term, serial), measured with the area weights and before the per-tet energy: 'vertex_ring' exits after 7 turns with max AMIPS 8.784 and 20724 front faces, 60 of them over the bar (the largest 1.355x) while every ring measure is within it (the largest 0.963x); 'face' exits after 7 turns with max AMIPS 7.814 and 23476 front faces. The debug frames carry the ring measure as point data, front_ring_ratio, in both modes (2D: on the _front.vtu chord mesh).

docs.title: sorted_marching
docs.text:
bool · default false

Execute the marching in decreasing order of edge length. Increases run time, may increase output mesh quality.

docs.title: save_offset_correspondence
docs.text:
bool · default false

2D and 3D, and only with optimize_offset false (the run refuses the combination with true). The output .msh carries the node field corr_input_vid, a scalar $NodeData entry for every vertex of the mesh (the retained envelope's own nodes, when the input has an EnvelopeSurface, carry none). The march splits every edge with exactly one endpoint on the input complex and so makes the offset vertices (vertex label 2, the vertices of the offset band that are not on the complex); for each such vertex the field holds the 0-based index of that edge's endpoint on the complex, the input-complex vertex the offset vertex was split off from. Every other vertex holds -1. The index is the output file's own: vertex k is the node with tag k + 1. The optimization splits, collapses and renumbers vertices and does not carry the field, hence the restriction. The prismatic_mesh component reads this file. 3D, memory route: an input that already carries corr_input_vid (an earlier offset's output, with its vid) keeps it, so offsets run one after another hand prismatic_mesh every band's correspondence. Each value holds while its offset vertex keeps its id and its star (its tets, by their corners), from which prismatic_mesh builds the prisms: construction only splits, and only near this run's input complex, so a carried star that changes means the two offsets touch, and the run throws. Without this key the incoming field is ignored, as is any on the .msh route, whose reader drops node data. Default false: the .msh has no node data.

docs.title: sphere_trace_target_rel_tol
docs.text:
float · default 0.01

In (0, 1). The marching's sphere trace stops at the first point where |d(x) - D| <= this x D, D being the distance the march traces to (target_distance, or half the maximum marchable distance under construction_mode max_marchable_fallback); the placed vertex is that close to that level set along the edge. Smaller is tighter and takes more steps (each step is longer than the tolerance, so at most edge length / (this x D) per edge).

docs.title: construction_mode
docs.text:
string · default "max_marchable_fallback" · one of max_marchable_fallback, midpoint_fallback

How the marching constructs the offset. Construction first measures the maximum marchable distance, the smallest distance from the input complex of the outer end of any marched edge (an edge with one end in the input complex and the other in the background). Every marched edge's inner end is on the complex, so the level set d = D crosses every marched edge for every D up to that distance. If target_distance is below it, every marched edge is split where d(x) = target_distance, found by sphere tracing from the complex end (to within sphere_trace_target_rel_tol). Otherwise: 'max_marchable_fallback' (the default) traces every marched edge to half the maximum marchable distance instead; 'midpoint_fallback' splits every marched edge at its midpoint. Either way target_distance itself is not changed: the optimization carries the offset surface out to it. Both dimensions.

docs.title: init_optimize
docs.text:
bool · default false

Default false, as the band-volume runs ran it. 2D and 3D. Construction measures the maximum marchable distance, the smallest distance from the input complex of the outer end of any marched edge (the largest target every marched edge can be traced to). If target_distance is below it, the init_optimize loop is not done: the offset is marched to the target and the loop runs with refinement as usual, and the log says so. If target_distance is not below it, every marched edge is split as construction_mode says (the default traces it to half the maximum marchable distance; midpoint_fallback splits it at its midpoint), the loop first converges under stencil_order with no refinement (the sizing field left as it is), without the final pass, and then the ordinary loop converges under the same stencil_order with its refinement, final pass and verdict. target_distance is never changed. The no-refinement loop's debug frames are led by i.

docs.title: repulsion_smoothing_passes
docs.text:
int · default 0 · min 0

2D and 3D. At most this many smoothing passes between the simplicial embedding and the march, so that the march can trace to target_distance itself. The march traces every marched edge (one end in the input complex, the other not) to target_distance only if every outer end is farther than it (the maximum marchable distance, see construction_mode); otherwise it falls back. The repulsion vertices are those outer ends -- the one ring of the input complex's vertices minus the complex -- that no input envelope holds. One per-cell energy holds before the march: the energy's AMIPS term (3D: see offset_amips_weight; 2D: w AMIPS, the 2D engine's quality, w = offset_amips_weight, as the front) plus, for each corner v of the cell (2D: face) that is a repulsion vertex joined in that cell to the input complex by a marched edge, O(v) = (max(0, 2 delta - d(v)) / front_conv)^2, delta = target_distance, d the Euclidean distance to the input complex. O is one-sided, so it pushes a vertex out and never pulls one in, and its target is 2 delta so that the march at delta splits each edge with room to spare (the construction's own fallback, half the maximum marchable distance, run backwards). Every vertex is smoothed against the sum of that energy over its ring, so a repulsion vertex's O(v) counts once for every ring cell that carries it; every other vertex is smoothed as in the loop. In 3D no move may raise the sum of the energy over the vertex's ring; in 2D a repulsion move has no veto and every other vertex keeps the veto on the max of the energy over its ring. The passes stop as soon as every outer end is farther than delta + front_conv, i.e. outside the tolerance band. Each pass logs the maximum marchable distance, the outer ends within delta + front_conv, delta and 2 delta, and the max AMIPS; with debug_output a frame repulsion_<k> follows each pass. 0 (the default) = off: no pass, no frame, no log line.

docs.title: repulsion_rounds
docs.text:
int · default 0 · min 0

2D and 3D. After the repulsion_smoothing_passes (if any) and before the march, at most this many rounds of the loop's operations: split, collapse and swap, each followed by its smoothing passes, shaped as interleaved_smoothing says. No refinement: the sizing field is never lowered, so every operation aims at the base edge length. No split of a marched edge (one end in the input complex): its midpoint would be a new outer end nearer the input. The collapses and swaps compare the per-tet energy of repulsion_smoothing_passes, repulsion terms included, as the loop's rules compare its energy. The input complex stays simplicially embedded, as the march needs it: a collapse or swap that would leave a cell off the complex whose complex vertices span an edge or face off the complex is refused. After every operation pass the construction labels are recomputed from the region tags, and the repulsion vertices follow the operations. Single-body offset_in or offset_out only (the embedding test reads the complex off the cells' labels); other selections, and in 2D a curve group, are refused with an error. The rounds stop as soon as every outer end is farther than target_distance + front_conv. Each round logs its operations' outcomes ([ops accounting], [swap reject], 3D only: the 2D engine has neither; the embedding refusals, which those counters have no name for, are counted on the round's own line), the maximum marchable distance and the max AMIPS; with debug_output a frame repulsion_round_<k> follows each round. The embedding test reads cells beyond an operation's lock, so run the rounds with num_threads 0. 0 (the default) = off.

docs.title: settle_stall_eps
docs.text:
float · default 0.1 · min 0.0

3D, EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_rule "surface" only (a non-default value under another rule is refused), with EXPERIMENTAL_settle_refinement. The settle test's stall threshold eps_stuck (Spencer 2026-10-27, HackMD "settlement option 2": TetWild's stuck test on the max offset error across stencil points instead of the max AMIPS across tets). O* = the max over every front face's stencil points (stencil_order, interior) of (d - target_distance)^2; a turn is settled when O* < front_conv^2 (every stencil point within the tolerance; his answer) or O*_prev - O* <= settle_stall_eps (O* - front_conv^2) -- TetOptimizerMesh::optimization_stalled()'s (prev - cur) <= stuck_refine_stall_eps (cur - target). A rise settles. Default 0.1, TetWild's stuck_refine_stall_eps default. The marking, halving and exit of a settled turn are EXPERIMENTAL_settle_mark's, unchanged.

docs.title: optimize_construction
docs.text:
bool · default true

3D, with optimize_offset (since 2026-10-21; replaces EXPERIMENTAL_construction_tetwild_run, EXPERIMENTAL_refine_construction and EXPERIMENTAL_refine_construction_factor, which the strict spec now refuses). true (the default): before the loop (and before an init_optimize loop), after the 'construction' frame, TetWild's own pass runs on the mesh as constructed (TopoOffsetTetMesh::optimize_construction_pass()). It starts from the sizing field at 1 everywhere: every vertex's sizing scalar is set to 1 first (nothing before the pass lowers it, so a vertex reset there is warned about), and the offset surface's field is not lowered. Every tracked surface is held: the offset surface in an envelope of eps half the distance the march traced it to (d_0 when growth_mode applies, else target_distance) -- in this pass only; the final TetWild pass holds it to envelope_size -- its vertices smoothed like any held vertex, pulled to and kept in that envelope; the domain wall, the input complex's boundary and every other region boundary in the envelope (envelope_size). TetWild's own rules decide: the smoother minimises the raw sum of AMIPS over the one-ring with TetWild's quality veto on the ring's max (TetOptimizerMesh::smooth_after()), and collapses and swaps are judged by the max of AMIPS^3 over the cells they change -- no band term, no summed energy rule, no split gate (EXPERIMENTAL_split_energy_gate), no damping, and no plastic medium whatever use_rest_pose says; TetWild's bare coarsening passes run before the first iteration and after the last. Up to max_iterations iterations of TetWild's operation groups, stopping once max AMIPS < stop_energy. Its operations carry the sizing field (a split's new vertex takes the mean of its edge's scalars, a collapse's survivor the smaller, sizing_collapse_min) and its stall refinement lowers it around the worst cells; the loop starts from the field the pass leaves, with the vertex order recomputed and, under use_rest_pose, the plastic rests stamped again. Logged as [optimize construction] (the envelopes, max AMIPS before and after, the sizing scalar's range after), plus '[energy step] turn 0 start' before it and '[energy step] turn 0 tetwild' after it; its debug frames are labelled cr0F<n>_<operation>, then cr0S_end for the mesh it hands to the loop (DEBUG_remote_output: cr0F_start, cr0F_it<k>). Ignored when optimize_offset is false. false: the loop starts on the mesh as constructed.

docs.title: growth_mode
docs.text:
string · default "none" · one of none, linear, smart, individual_op_reject

3D (since 2026-10-21; "linear" is the former EXPERIMENTAL_incremental_growth, which the strict spec now refuses with EXPERIMENTAL_incremental_growth_steps). How the loop grows the offset to target_distance from where the march put it. Growth acts only when the march traces the front below the target: construction_mode "max_marchable_fallback" (the default) with target_distance not below the maximum marchable distance M traces every marched edge to d_0 = M / 2 (see construction_mode). Not done -- the loop running once at target_distance as usual -- when the march traces to target_distance itself (the target below M), marches nothing, or cannot trace (a marched edge ends on the complex, so every marched edge is split at its midpoint; a warning); the log says which. Every loop below is the loop as configured, at its own target: the same energy (its band term reads that target), smoothing, settle test, refinement and exit, and the same front_conv (front_conv_rel is relative to the configured target_distance); before each loop the offset field, the per-piece fields and the exact band integral are rebuilt at its target; the mesh and its sizing field carry over, as does every length fixed when the parameters were read (envelope_size, the base edge length, min_edge_length). "none" (the default): one loop, at target_distance. "linear": the loop runs N + 1 times (N = linear_growth_steps): stage k = 0, 1, ..., N at the target d_0 + k (target_distance - d_0) / N, so stage 0 at d_0 and stage N at target_distance exactly, each up to max_rounds turns. Stages 0 to N - 1 each run until the loop converges and end there, without the final TetWild pass or the verdict; stage N is the ordinary loop, with both. A stage before the last that does not converge within max_rounds turns stops the run: the later stages are not run, and the verdict and the report measure the mesh that stage left against target_distance. Logged: one [incremental growth] line at construction, '======== [incremental growth] stage k / N' before each stage; each stage numbers its turns from 1, and its debug frames are led by g<k> (stage N's by nothing). "smart": first the loop at d_0 (level 0), up to max_rounds turns; if it does not converge the run stops with an error. The mesh is then stored in memory (TopoOffsetTetMesh::take_snapshot()) and an attempt runs at target_distance: the loop for up to smart_growth_attempts turns. An attempt succeeds when the loop converges and no offset face is folded at that point (its normal, out of the band, more than foldover_angle from grad d; checked once, on the converged mesh). A failed attempt puts the stored mesh back (restore_snapshot()), and the next is tried halfway: after j failed attempts from the same converged distance d_b the target is d_b + (target_distance - d_b) / 2^j. A success below target_distance makes that target the new d_b: the mesh is stored again and the next attempt is at target_distance again. smart_growth_max_fails failed attempts from one d_b stop the run with an error. The attempt that succeeds at target_distance ends the run as the ordinary loop does (the final TetWild pass when max AMIPS >= stop_energy, the verdict); an attempt at a smaller target ends without them. Logged: one [smart growth] line at construction, '======== [smart growth] level L ...' before level 0 and before each attempt, one result line per attempt (converged or not, folded faces), a 'reverted' line after each failure and a summary at the end; each loop numbers its turns from 1, and the debug frames are led by s0 (level 0) and s<L>a<A> (level L's attempt A; a failed attempt's frames stay). "individual_op_reject" (since 2026-10-21): the loop at d_0 (up to max_rounds turns), then the loop at target_distance, nothing between -- "linear" with one step, logged and framed as it, and stopped the same way when the loop at d_0 does not converge -- and in every loop of the run (not in a TetWild pass: the optimize_construction pass and the final pass run as usual) each collapse, flip of the offset surface and smoothing move is refused when it raises the number of folded offset faces among the faces it changes (folded: the face's normal, out of the band, more than foldover_angle from grad d at its centroid; a collapse: the faces through its two ends before against those through the survivor after; a flip: its two old faces against its two new ones; a smoothing move: the faces through the vertex before and after). An operation near an existing fold may keep or remove it. Splits are not checked. Logged per operation group as [op reject] (collapses, flips, smoothing moves refused). Refused with construction_mode "midpoint_fallback" (it never traces below the target) and with init_optimize true (both decide the loops after such a march).

docs.title: linear_growth_steps
docs.text:
int · default 4 · min 1

3D, growth_mode "linear" (since 2026-10-21; was EXPERIMENTAL_incremental_growth_steps): N, the number of equal steps from the distance the march traced the front to, d_0, to target_distance. The loop runs N + 1 stages, at d_0 + k (target_distance - d_0) / N for k = 0, 1, ..., N (see growth_mode); N = 1 is two loops, at d_0 and at target_distance. Must be >= 1; a value other than the default with another growth_mode is refused with an error. 4 (the default): stages at d_0, then a quarter, half, three quarters and all of the way from d_0 to target_distance.

docs.title: smart_growth_attempts
docs.text:
int · default 2 · min 1

3D, growth_mode "smart" (since 2026-10-21): the turns each attempt toward a larger target gets to converge (level 0, the loop at d_0, has max_rounds). Must be >= 1; a value other than the default with another growth_mode is refused with an error. 2 (the default).

docs.title: smart_growth_max_fails
docs.text:
int · default 10 · min 1

3D, growth_mode "smart" (since 2026-10-21): how many attempts from one converged distance d_b may fail -- each failure halves the step toward target_distance -- before the run stops with an error. Counted per converged distance: a success starts the count again. Must be >= 1; a value other than the default with another growth_mode is refused with an error. 10 (the default): the last attempt from d_b is at d_b + (target_distance - d_b) / 2^9.

docs.title: foldover_angle
docs.text:
float · default 30.0 · min 0.0 · max 180.0

3D. The angle, in degrees, above which an offset-surface face counts as a foldover: the angle between the face's normal, oriented out of the band (away from its band cell's fourth corner), and the field's normal, the unit gradient of the distance d to the input complex at the face's centroid (TopoOffsetTetMesh::front_face_field_angle()). 0 is a face facing exactly along the field, 180 one facing straight back at the input. A face whose angle cannot be measured (no band cell, zero area, or a zero gradient) is not a foldover. Read by the debug frames -- each _off file carries the per-face cell fields field_normal_angle (the angle; NaN where unmeasurable) and field_angle_foldover (1 over this threshold, else 0; named offset_foldover until 2026-10-26, when offset_foldover became the flag of the two faces of every real fold, the real folds of EXPERIMENTAL_exit_no_folds); the per-vertex offset_foldover field the frames carried until 2026-10-20 (an endpoint of a front edge whose two faces met within 30 degrees) is gone -- and by the end of the run, where a warning [foldover] counts the folded offset faces of the mesh about to be written, with the worst angle and where it is. In the optimization this test is read by growth_mode "smart"'s fold-free check, growth_mode "individual_op_reject"'s operation rule, and EXPERIMENTAL_exit_no_folds, which holds the exit only for a real fold with a face over this angle; nowhere else. A second, diagnostic-only field pair on the _off files, dihedral_angle (the band-side dihedral across the face's most folded edge, 180 flat) and offset_foldover_dihedral (1 where it is below this angle or above 360 minus it), uses the same threshold and decides nothing (since 2026-10-21). 2D still labels vertices by its own rule. 30 (the default).

docs.title: save_vtu
docs.text:
bool · default false

Save .vtu of output mesh

docs.title: phi_grid_resolution
docs.text:
int · default 0

Samples per side of the grid the smooth offset potential is written on, as <output>_phi.vtu, for the viewer. 0 disables it. The grid is the plane through the box centre normal to the box's shortest extent (the whole domain when the domain is planar). Carries phi, phi_residual_length and euclidean_distance per vertex; warp by phi to see the field as a height surface. Written only when the optimization runs (optimize_offset true): the potential is built for it alone.

docs.title: preallocation_factor
docs.text:
float · default 6.0 · min 1.0

Mesh storage (connectivity and attributes) is preallocated to this factor times the live element count at init and at consolidation. Operations take fresh slots from that headroom and are retried once it is exhausted. Lower it for pure-decimation runs and raise it for aggressive refinement; the offset refines aggressively, so a run whose log carries [slots] warnings is dropping the very splits the criterion asked for.

docs.title: num_smoothing_passes
docs.text:
int · default 2

Smoothing passes after the ONE combined split+collapse+swap round when interleaved_smoothing is OFF (the default is ON since 2026-09-28) -- in the loop (3D since 2026-09-25, 2D since 2026-10-05), and in the shared optimization loop, which in this component runs only in the TetWild passes, 2D and 3D alike. The default turn is therefore split, collapse, swap, then 2 smoothing passes. Not read when interleaving is on: the count is then interleaved_smoothing_passes, everywhere. TriWild's key and TriWild's default.

docs.title: length_rel
docs.text:
float · default 0.05

Target edge length relative to the bounding box diagonal. Used to bound which edges edge collapse is allowed to touch (only edges shorter than 4/5 of this length are collapsed). Ignored if length >= 0.

docs.title: length
docs.text:
float · default -1.0

Target edge length (absolute). If < 0, computed from length_rel.

docs.title: stop_energy
docs.text:
float · default 100.0

Target AMIPS quality for the elements. Default 100, matching the tetwild component -- the final TetWild pass is TriWild/TetWild and stops where they stop. Do not lower it far: a target the operation set cannot deliver turns the split pass into an unbounded refiner. Edge collapse will not push an already-on-target region's quality back above this. In 3D it also scales the energy's AMIPS term, offset_amips_weight * vol * (AMIPS / stop_energy)^3 (see offset_amips_weight).

docs.title: max_iterations
docs.text:
int · default 80

Cap on the shared TriWild/TetWild loop, which runs only in the TetWild passes: the final pass, and in 3D the construction pass (optimize_construction). The loop exits as soon as max AMIPS is under stop_energy, so this is an upper bound.

docs.title: interleaved_smoothing
docs.text:
bool · default true

Run split, collapse and swap as three separate rounds with interleaved_smoothing_passes smoothing passes after each, instead of one combined round followed by num_smoothing_passes. DEFAULT TRUE since 2026-09-28 (it was false from 2026-09-25, when the smoothing was 63% of a turn and 5 of its 6 passes near no-ops; the single energy, the exact Hessian and the relative gradient tolerance made a front solve 2-3 Newton iterations instead of 10). Measured on the cube with the single energy, mix vetos: serial target 1e-2 / tolerance 1e-4, combined 7 turns / 22396 faces / 215 s, interleaved 6 / 20102 / 203 s; 10 threads, combined 7-9 turns / 22260-25416 faces / 55-98 s, interleaved 6-7 / 19870-21186 / 60-75 s; 10 threads 1e-3 / 5e-5 (neither resolved in 10 turns), combined 95040 faces / 330 s, interleaved 75826 / 390 s. The gain is in the late turns: the front the exit test judges has been re-placed after every operation, so fewer vertices are over the bar and halved.

docs.title: interleaved_smoothing_passes
docs.text:
int · default 2

Smoothing passes after each operation group (split, collapse, swap) when interleaved_smoothing is on -- in the shared TriWild/TetWild loop (the TetWild passes) and in the loop. Default 2, against the shared engine's own 1: each smoothing pass is one placement sweep of the front, so at one pass per group the front contracts about half as fast for the same final result.

docs.title: colored_smoothing
docs.text:
bool · default false

Parallel smoothing (num_threads > 0) by color class: the vertices are split into classes of pairwise non-adjacent vertices, smoothed one class after another, each class fully in parallel without locks. The result does not depend on the number of threads. false: the locked, partitioned smoothing pass, whose result depends on the thread schedule. Serial runs (num_threads 0) are the same either way. Default false for the offset: on the Geneva mechanism base (inward, target 1e-3 of the largest body, 2026-10-12) the colored order left the front folded -- 129-179 vertices flagged by offset_foldover after turn 1 against 0-6 with the partitioned pass, one thread or six, the same count with one thread as with six, so it is the order and not a race; on the outward cube with every other key at its default (10 threads, 2026-10-13) colored smoothing did not resolve in 40 turns and left 51 flagged vertices standing from turn 15, where the partitioned pass resolved at turn 20 with none in any frame.

docs.title: pre_smooth
docs.text:
bool · default false

The loop only, not the final pass. true: before the first turn, run one smoothing block on the mesh as constructed -- the same block each operation group is followed by: num_smoothing_passes sweeps under interleaved_smoothing false and interleaved_smoothing_passes under true (the default), 2D and 3D alike -- (2D: with the plastic rests stamped before it and the released-boundary envelope refreshed after it), so the front is carried toward the level set once before the first split pass measures it. false (the default): the loop starts with turn 1's split pass on the constructed mesh.

docs.title: coarsen_pass
docs.text:
bool · default false

Run the post-optimization coarsening pass, as TriWild and TetWild do. It trades elements for nothing but the guarantee that the result is still good, so topological_offset holds it to an absolute bar -- both AMIPS and the offset residual inside tolerance after each collapse -- rather than the non-degrading bar the main loop uses. Off by default: the pass can dominate total runtime, and being the last thing to run before the final convergence check, anything it degrades is reported as a quality failure rather than a coarsening one. 3D: EXPERIMENTAL_coarsen_guard picks what judges a coarsening collapse (the absolute bar above is its default, "bar").

docs.title: coarsen_unbounded
docs.text:
bool · default true

Coarsen as far as the quality guarantee allows, instead of stopping at the target edge length. The pass then answers how few elements can hold this max energy, which is more aggressive than it sounds because the answer ignores how big the elements become; measured over the registered models it roughly doubles the cell reduction while raising max energy on none of them. On by default. Turned off, it leaves alone any edge already at or past the collapse threshold, since collapsing it only makes its neighbours longer. The sizing field is deliberately not applied either way: honouring it here would leave the pass unable to undo refinement that turned out to be unnecessary.

docs.title: coarsen_max_rounds
docs.text:
int · default 2

Cap on the coarsen/smooth alternation; the pass also stops as soon as a round accepts no collapse. A round does not exist to finish what the previous one started: within a round the collapse pass already runs to a fixed point, so repeating the collapse alone finds nothing. What a round adds is the global smoothing in between, which moves that fixed point. Returns decay fast, and the default of two carries the large majority of the coarsening for a fraction of what the later rounds would cost.

docs.title: coarsen_global_smoothing_passes
docs.text:
int · default 1

Ordinary whole-mesh smoothing passes run between coarsening rounds. This is what makes a second round worth running at all -- see coarsen_max_rounds -- so setting it to 0 collapses the rounds to one.

docs.title: coarsen_smooth_ring
docs.text:
int · default 1

How far the local smoothing after each coarsening collapse reaches, in rings; the pass locks one ring wider than this. Deliberately 1 rather than TriWild's and TetWild's 2: a smaller ball perturbs less per collapse, so more collapses clear the offset's absolute coarsening bar.

docs.title: coarsen_local_smoothing_passes
docs.text:
int · default 0

Smoothing sweeps over the ring inside each candidate coarsening collapse, before its max energy is measured, so the collapse is judged on a relaxed neighbourhood rather than on the configuration it lands in. 0 by default: the ring is large enough that even two sweeps cost hundreds of nonlinear solves per candidate, and turning it off costs almost no cell reduction because the pass runs to a fixed point and finds another candidate instead. At 0 the only relaxation is the global smoothing between rounds, which has no per-operation accept test of its own -- see the forced quality veto in TetOptimizerMesh::coarsen_mesh().

docs.title: stuck_refine_stall_eps
docs.text:
float · default 0.1

Fire the sizing refinement when an iteration's improvement is small next to the distance the metric still has to cover: (prev - cur) <= stall_eps * (cur - target). 0 means only when it does not improve at all.

docs.title: stuck_refine_cooldown
docs.text:
int · default 1

Iterations to skip after a sizing refinement before another may fire. Default 1, matching the tetwild component: the refined sizing needs one split/collapse round to act before the stall detector can fairly judge it. 0 allows one every iteration.

docs.title: stuck_refine_num_worst
docs.text:
int · default 0

How many worst faces seed the refinement. 0 means every face above the filter threshold, which is TriWild's default.

docs.title: stuck_refine_rings
docs.text:
int · default 0

Vertex rings grown around each seeded face before the sizing scalar is lowered.

docs.title: stuck_refine_factor
docs.text:
float · default 0.5

Multiplicative reduction of the per-vertex sizing scalar per refinement.

docs.title: stuck_refine_min_scalar
docs.text:
float · default 0.001

Floor on the per-vertex sizing scalar.

docs.title: stuck_refine_gradation
docs.text:
float · default 2.0

Neighbouring sizing scalars may differ by at most this factor. The smoothing only ever lowers a scalar, spreading refinement outward. <= 1 disables it.

docs.title: stuck_refine_force_split
docs.text:
bool · default true

On a stall, also split each seeded face's longest edge once, bypassing the length gate and without touching the sizing field.

docs.title: sizing_collapse_min
docs.text:
bool · default true

What the surviving vertex of a collapse keeps as its sizing scalar. true (the default): the smaller of the two, which is the shared engine's rule. false: its own scalar, restored after the base collapse. The min rule carries substantially more vertices and lengthens the placement loop where the front travels, because the offset's sizing follows a moving front and has to relax behind it, which a scalar that only ever falls cannot do.

docs.title: min_edge_length
docs.text:
float · default -1.0

l_min: the shortest edge the sizing field may ask for, in absolute units. If < 0, derived as min_edge_length_rel * target_distance -- tied to the offset distance rather than the bounding box, because the offset is what has to be resolved. This is a floor on REFINEMENT, so raising it makes the offset coarser (paper Fig. 18).

docs.title: min_edge_length_rel
docs.text:
float · default -1.0

l_min as a multiple of target_distance, used when min_edge_length is negative. Negative (the default) derives it from the envelope epsilon, envelope_size -- the offset surface's envelope eps too since 2026-10-20, when offset_envelope (until then this floor's source) was removed -- as a multiple of target_distance: TetWild's own floor (cap the sizing field below by the envelope eps, Sec 3.2) stated in the offset's units, since the front is only held to within eps and edges shorter than eps cannot buy fidelity. A pure anti-runaway rail, far below the chord length any tolerance actually needs.

docs.title: min_sizing_scalar
docs.text:
float · default 0.01

Lower bound for the per-vertex sizing field (see max_sizing_scalar). Refinement stops once a vertex's sizing scalar reaches this fraction of the base target length.

docs.title: max_sizing_scalar
docs.text:
float · default 1.0

Upper bound for the per-vertex sizing field, as a multiplier on the target edge length (splitting_l2/collapsing_l2). 1.0 means never coarser than the base target length.

docs.title: sizing_gradation
docs.text:
float · default 2.0

Gradation cap for the sizing field: neighbouring vertices' sizing scalars may differ by at most this factor. After each refinement pass the refined vertices' lower sizing scalar is propagated outward -- monotone, only ever lowering a neighbour's scalar -- so the mesh does not jump straight from fine to coarse. <= 1 disables gradation. Only read when sizing_gradation_mode is 'ring'.

docs.title: sizing_gradation_mode
docs.text:
string · default "ring" · one of ring, distance

How a lowered sizing scalar spreads to the vertices around it, at every place the offset lowers the field (the sag rule, the stuck refine). 'ring' (the default): the base gradation_smooth_sizing -- walk outward over mesh neighbours, capping each neighbour at sizing_gradation times the scalar it came from, so the field grades by mesh rings and a fine seed in a coarse mesh drags a shell of rings down with it. 'distance': TetWild's adjust_sizing_field gradation -- walk outward from the seeds and multiply every vertex within R = 1.8 l of its nearest seed by the linear ramp 0.5 + 0.5 dist / R (halved next to a seed, untouched at R), stopping at R; the seeds keep the value they were just given and nothing outside the ball changes. The refinement then reaches a seed geometrically through the split pass (each split child takes the mean of its parents' scalars) instead of by rings, so a fine target stays local to the seed however coarse the mesh around it is.

docs.title: split_high_valence_threshold
docs.text:
int · default 0

Incident-cell count above which a vertex in a split edge's link accepts only one valence-increasing split per pass, or 0 to disable. Spreads refinement instead of letting it pile onto one vertex.

docs.title: project_line_search_steps
docs.text:
int · default 12

Bisections tried by the projected line search before it gives up on a vertex: the step along the Newton direction is halved this many times, each candidate projected onto the input, and the first that does not invert and lowers the worst incident element is taken.

docs.title: project_line_search_nested_steps
docs.text:
int · default 0

After the projected line search gives up, revisit each candidate and bisect between the interpolated point and its projection this many times, taking the longest step toward the input that still does not invert and still lowers the worst element. Lets a vertex whose one-ring cannot tolerate a full projection still travel toward the input, instead of being refused every pass from the same place. 0 disables the pass.

docs.title: offset_amips_weight
docs.text:
float · default 1.0 · min 0.0

Under EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_rule "surface" w multiplies the AMIPS term only (the offset term is unweighted, 2026-10-28): w is the ratio of the two terms. The weight w of AMIPS in the per-cell energy. 3D: THE energy E is the sum over the cells of tet_energy (TopoOffsetTetMesh::tet_energy()) = (w / stop_energy^3) vol AMIPS^3 (AMIPS against the cell's rest shape for a plastic cell under use_rest_pose), plus for a band cell b = vol * min over the input triangles P of the mean over its four corners of (d_P - target_distance) / target_distance, d_P the distance to triangle P alone (EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_rule "corner_bound", the default; "exact" takes the cell's closed-form integral of (d - target_distance) / target_distance); MAX_ENERGY where the engine cannot score the cell's AMIPS. b is the cell's part of the integral over the band of (d - target_distance) / target_distance, as an upper bound that no split raises (d_P is convex and d <= d_P). Both terms are volumes, so E converges under refinement; a cell at the stop energy costs about w vol in AMIPS. Every operation compares the SUM of tet_energy over the cells it changes, before against after: a collapse may not raise it (a tie passes); a swap -- 3-2, 4-4, 5-6, the face swap, and the 4-4 / 5-6 case search and the face swap's gate that pick and gate the cells it makes -- must strictly lower it; a smoothing move may not raise it over the vertex's ring; a split is judged only under EXPERIMENTAL_split_energy_gate. The engine's own AMIPS^3 rules for collapses and swaps are off. The smoother minimises the vertex's part of E: the AMIPS term over its ring and, unless an input envelope holds the vertex, the band term of its band cells. Needs one input region, an input complex of triangles only, and offset_field 'euclidean' (refused otherwise). Why the corner bound with the min over all triangles, and why a vertex held on the input carries no band term: see TopoOffsetTetMesh::band_cell_term() and smoothing_extra_energy(). DEFAULT 1, the weight the band-volume runs used (the eight-case suite of 2026-10-09 among them). The default before, 1e-4, was chosen 2026-09-30 for the energy this replaced (AMIPS^3 plus the front faces' squared measures, compared by maxima); here it would make the AMIPS term 1e-10 vol AMIPS^3. 2D: the same weight multiplies AMIPS (the 2D engine's cell quality) in tri_energy = w AMIPS + the offset terms of the front chords, and in the 2D front smoother.

docs.title: smoothing_mode
docs.text:
string · default "projected" · one of projected, exact

How smoothing places a surface vertex. 'projected': smooth with AMIPS alone as if interior, then walk back toward the start projecting each candidate onto the input; accept the first projected candidate that does not invert and strictly lowers the worst incident element, else do not move. Lands exactly on the input; no weights. 'exact': minimize w_amips * AMIPS + (1-w_amips) * (d/eps)^2 with the true region-wise Hessian of the distance to the piecewise-linear input; sliding is free where the input is flat, held at corners, constrained along edges and curve segments. Rests a w_amips-proportional distance off the input.

docs.title: w_amips
docs.text:
float · default 0.0001

Relative weight of the AMIPS quality term against the envelope term during smoothing of envelope-held vertices (the engine's input-surface envelope term); the envelope weight is 1 - w_amips. The front objective does not read it, in 2D or 3D: in 3D the objective is the vertex's part of the energy (see offset_amips_weight); in 2D AMIPS enters at offset_amips_weight and the offset term at 1 / (front_conv / target_distance)^2, i.e. in units of the tolerance -- the two parts of the per-cell energy.

docs.title: perform_sanity_checks
docs.text:
bool · default false

Check after every operation pass that no element is inverted and no tracked-surface simplex left its envelope. Slow; for debugging.

docs.title: use_rest_pose
docs.text:
bool · default false

3D. Which AMIPS the energy (see offset_amips_weight) uses for the cells outside the offset band and the input complex during the loop; the band and the complex are always measured against the regular tet. true: the plastic medium -- each such cell's AMIPS term is vol A^3 with A its AMIPS against its rest shape, stamped when the loop starts, after every smoothing pass (between passes and after the last, not before the first), and, in the operations, on every cell a split or a swap creates or a collapse changes, before that operation's energy rule reads it; so every rule reads up-to-date rests, and a smoothing pass resists only what it moves itself. When an operation's cells before and after are all plastic (no band or input-complex cell), its energy is exactly the same before and after (A = 3 everywhere, one total volume), which floating point does not reproduce (TopoOffsetTetMesh::plastic_tie()). The equality is taken instead: such a swap is refused outright, and such a collapse is not gated by the energy, only by the length gate, the inversion test and the other refusals. Logged per group as [plastic tie]. The rules (tet_energy()), the swap candidates and the smoother all read the same term. false (the default): the regular tet for every cell. Off in the final pass either way. Envelopes, either way: during the loop only the domain wall and the input complex's boundary are held (envelope_size); every other region boundary is a tracked face nothing holds, and is held, as the loop left it, only in a TetWild pass. Replaces deform_others (removed 2026-10-13; 2D hard-wires its old default, false, until the 2D port).

docs.title: envelope
docs.text:
string · default ""

Memory route only: the name of the input mesh that holds the envelope surface of a tagged mesh input -- the envelope mesh simwild returns with its result. On the file route, the .msh input's own EnvelopeSurface group plays this role, and this option is ignored.

docs.title: input_dir
docs.text:
string · default ""

Directory where the input files are located. This is injected by the application and should not be set by the user.

docs.title: num_threads
docs.text:
int · default 0

Number of threads used for parallel execution (smoothing, edge collapse). 0 means single-threaded.

docs.title: log_file
docs.text:
string · default ""

Logs are not just printed on the terminal but also saved in this file.

docs.title: report
docs.text:
string · default ""

A JSON file that stores information about the result and the method execution, e.g., runtime.

docs.title: Debug options
docs.text:
Diagnostics: slow checks and extra output files. (4)

DEBUG_stencil · bool · default false

DEBUG (2026-10-29), 3D, with DEBUG_output (or DEBUG_remote_output; refused otherwise). true: every debug frame also writes <frame>_stencil.vtu (and <output>_stencil.pvd lists them), one VTK vertex cell per stencil point of every offset face (offset_surface_faces() order times the face stencil: stencil_order, EXPERIMENTAL_stencil_type; a point shared by two faces appears once per face), with point fields stencil_error r^2 (r = (d - target_distance) / target_distance), error_over_bound (d - target_distance)^2 / front_conv^2 (>= 1 out of tolerance), signed_error r, distance_over_target 1 + r, sq_error (d - target_distance)^2 (its max is O*, the "surface" rule's settle metric), face and point. Not written before the loop's offset potential exists, nor for a mesh without offset faces. false (the default): no _stencil file.

DEBUG_output · bool · default false

Write debug VTU frames of the evolving mesh, in both dimensions: one frame after every operation pass and every smoothing pass, as sequential <output>_NNNNN.vtu files so ParaView loads them as one time series, plus <output>frames.txt carrying one 'NNNNN<tab>r<turn><phase><pass><op>' line per frame, which the viewer scripts read for their labels; in 3D also <output>_energy.txt, one 'NNNNN<tab>label<tab>band term<tab>AMIPS term' line per frame, the energy's two parts (see offset_amips_weight). Expect hundreds of frames on a real model; observational only, the frames cannot change the run.

DEBUG_remote_output · bool · default false

DEBUG (2026-10-20), 3D. A sparser debug-frame schedule for runs on a machine short on disk space. true OVERRIDES DEBUG_output: it is set to true, so everything debug output computes runs as usual (the frames carry the same fields, <output>_input_complex.vtu, <output>_energy.txt and <output>_frames.txt are written), but frames are written only at these points: the mesh as constructed, just before the optimization (label 'construction'); at the start of each TetWild pass ('<prefix>r<turn>F_start': optimize_construction's before the loop, the final pass after it) and after each of its iterations ('<prefix>r<turn>F_it<k>'); after the construction TetWild pass, before the loop (its end frame); after every turn of the loop ('<prefix>r<turn>S_end': one frame per split / smooth / collapse / smooth / swap / smooth cycle, after the turn's refinement; every growth stage and the init_optimize loop included); and the final mesh ('final', after the final pass when one runs). Not written: the input, the construction stages before the constructed mesh, the repulsion passes, and every per-operation and per-smoothing-pass frame. false (the default): DEBUG_output decides, with its usual frames.

DEBUG_crossings · bool · default false

Log-only: after every operation pass and every smoothing pass, count the front vertices whose ring measure crossed the bar (from <= 1 to > 1, and back), plus new vertices already over it; inside the front smoother, classify each accepted move whose ring-measure crossing it caused as the moved vertex's own or a front neighbour's. Changes no result; costs an exit-measure evaluation per pass and a local one per front move. 2D and 3D.

docs.title: Experimental options
docs.text:
Under development: they may change or go away. (14)

EXPERIMENTAL_stencil_type · string · default "subdivision" · one of subdivision, interior, fem

3D (2026-10-28, Spencer: "standard fem triangle points"). Which points stencil_order's face stencil holds. "subdivision" (the default): the corners plus the subdivision lattice described under stencil_order, which the face measures read before this key existed (order 0 the corners alone). "interior" (2026-10-27, Spencer: the surface integral's stencil, every point interior): the strictly interior lattice (i, j, l) / (k + 2), i, j, l >= 1, k (k + 1) / 2 points -- 1 (the centroid), 3, 6, 10, 15 for k = 1..5 -- none on an edge or a corner. "fem": the nodes of the degree-k Lagrange triangle, the lattice (i, j, l) / k with i + j + l = k, i, j, l >= 0, (k + 1) (k + 2) / 2 points -- order 1 the three corners, order 2 the corners and the edge midpoints, order 3 the corners, two points per edge and the centroid; 3, 6, 10, 15, 21 for k = 1..5. The points are weighted by their LUMPED AREA WEIGHTS (Spencer, 2026-10-28: "the area weights are split up properly"; no key): the composite trapezoid rule on the face cut into k^2 sub-triangles whose corners are the points, so a point carries 1 / (3 k^2) of the face's area at a corner, 1 / k^2 at an edge point and 2 / k^2 inside (order 1: a third each); a face's term is its area times the weighted mean of its points. A corner or edge point is shared with the neighbouring faces and gathers its weight from each, one third of the area of the sub-triangles around it. The weights are positive and exact for affine functions, so the energy's offset term converges to L int (d - delta)^2 / front_conv^2 dS at second order in the point spacing h / k, under mesh refinement and under a higher order alike (the interior stencil's plain mean converges under mesh refinement but only at first order as the order rises). "interior" and "fem" need stencil_order >= 1 (refused otherwise); their points are weighted as said, "subdivision"'s and "interior"'s by a plain mean. Read everywhere the face stencil is: EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_rule "surface"'s face term (the energy, its operation rules, the front solve), its O* settle test and O_g, every 3D face measure (ring and face measures, settle_mark "rms"), the face measures' mean weighted the same way, and the debug frames' _stencil file (DEBUG_stencil) (one point per face and stencil point, so a shared point appears once per face holding it; the O* max reads no weight). 2D does not read it.

EXPERIMENTAL_split_energy_gate · bool · default false

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-09), 3D. Every split of the optimisation loop (not the march's) is committed only if the energy E, summed over the cells it changes -- the parents before, the children after -- strictly falls, judged right after the split and before any smoothing; otherwise it is rolled back.
