A split never raises the energy's band term, so a split passes where the bound tightens by more than the AMIPS term rises (bisecting a well-shaped tet makes worse-shaped children), and is refused where the bound is already exact. Strict, since every split adds cells. What proposes splits is unchanged (the sizing field and its refinement). false (the default) = splits are not judged by the energy.

EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_rule · string · default "corner_bound" · one of corner_bound, exact, front_flux, exact_swept, surface

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-12), 3D. The band term b(t) of a band cell in the energy (see offset_amips_weight; TopoOffsetTetMesh::band_cell_term()), the cell's part of the integral over the band of (d - target_distance) / target_distance. "corner_bound" (the default): vol times the min, over all input triangles P, of the mean of (d_P - target_distance) / target_distance over the cell's four corners, d_P the distance to triangle P alone: an upper bound on the cell's part (d <= d_P, and the convex d_P lies below its linear interpolant) that no split raises (a child can use its parent's minimiser, whose finer interpolant lies lower); exact where one triangle's distance is affine on the cell. "exact": J_t / target_distance, J_t = int_t (d - target_distance) dV in closed form (ExactBandIntegral, a C++ port of the Python reference exact_mesh.integrate_mesh): the cell is cut by the local regions of the input's faces, edges and vertices into convex pieces on which d is one plane, line or point distance, each integrated exactly (Euler's theorem for homogeneous integrands and the divergence theorem on the faces; two convergent series with explicit tail bounds for faces nearly parallel to an input edge, stopped at each edge's own ratio). Where the border between two competing features' regions is curved (a face and an edge, or an edge and a vertex, inside one piece: "rule (a)") the piece takes the smaller of their integrals, an upper bound: 0.15-0.35% of the band volume on Thingi 100026, 0.01% on the cylinder, none on the cube and prism. The front smoother descends the same J with its exact gradient and Hessian in the moving vertex (Reynolds' transport theorem over the cell's faces through it); on a rule-(a) piece they are the bound's, and at a kink of d lying on a cell face the Hessian is the one-sided limit for the vertex moving into the cell. A split leaves the band's sum of J unchanged up to rounding and rule (a). Measured (mac-mini, 2026-10-12) against the Python on the 1020 stored band cells of five cases and 21160 random band cells: J agrees to 1.4e-12 relative (the problem's own conditioning: the Python's spread over the 24 corner orders of the same cells is as large), gradient and Hessian to 7e-11 (two of 4800 corner evaluations at 6e-6 in the Hessian, a cell face on an input edge where both are 2e-6 off the one-sided finite difference). Cost per cell: value 2.4-6 us, value with gradient and Hessian 3-43 us, against the corner bound's 0.5-1 us. Cube outward, 3 turns, serial, without refinement, against "corner_bound", the config otherwise the same (measured 2026-10-12 on ee18e19a1d, before held positions were picked by E): turns took 26.7 / 7.5 / 6.2 s against 6.7 / 2.9 / 2.5 s (smoothing 30.6 s against 5.3 s, mean Newton iterations 2.09 against 2.16); no smoothing pass raised E; every split changed the band term by at most 8e-15 relative (the corner bound's: up to 1.3e-3, the bound tightening), the in-loop check that the integral is exact; max AMIPS 16 against 39, the ring measure's max 12.8 against 5.1 bars (worst vertices near the cube's corners). "front_flux" (2026-10-13): the same J_t for every cell the operations, the veto and the energy read ("exact"'s value; a cell's part of the front form is J_t by the divergence theorem), and the front smoother's band term in the front form: per input feature (face, edge, vertex) a field G with div G = d - target_distance, tangent to the feature's region planes and 0 on the input (face (d^2/2 - delta d) n, edge (d/3 - delta/2)(x - its projection on the edge line), vertex (d/4 - delta/3)(x - v)), so the band integral is the flux of G through the band's boundary faces plus, per cell, the jump D_t of G.n across the bisectors (where two features are nearest) inside it. The vertex's band term is the flux through the band's boundary faces through it plus D_t of its flagged band cells, divided by target_distance: "exact"'s term up to a constant in the vertex position (the flux through the faces not holding it). Its gradient is the sum over those faces of n int_f (d - delta) phi dA (phi the vertex's hat function; Reynolds' transport theorem), its one-vertex Hessian the derivative of that, with no D_t term (d is Lipschitz). D_t is computed only for a cell flagged from the input alone: the overlaps of two features' regions within 2 target_distance of the input (and on the offset side of both), in a box tree; a cell whose bound on d exceeds that reach is flagged too; a false flag gives D_t = 0 exactly. Each piece of a face or cell is labelled with its nearest feature exactly (the exact range of the difference of squared distances, a quadratic, over the piece; planar bisectors split it); a curved bisector (face-edge, face-vertex, edge-vertex, skew edges) that changes sign on a piece is an error: the run stops with the feature pair and the position, as no approximation is made ("exact" bounds such a piece, rule (a)). The offset side as "exact": only the parts on the offset side of the input count. The exit test is unchanged. Measured (laptop, 2026-10-14, cube outward, target 1e-2, bar 1e-4, serial): the first smoothing pass matches "exact" to rounding (same accepted and refused moves; the energy after each turn-1 group equal to 10 digits); front_flux exited resolved at turn 13 in 603 s, "exact" ran its 15 turns unresolved in 1691 s (sharing the machine for its first 8 turns); one evaluation of the band part of a front vertex (value, gradient, Hessian), median / p90 over the front vertices of three band states (turn 1 after the split, a stored band, the last turn): corner_bound 6-7 / 11-17 us, "exact" 55-238 / 424-809 us, front_flux 25-150 / 193-508 us; the value alone, front_flux 25-65 us against "exact" 19-32 us (the edge flux needs a weighted face moment of the line distance, which only the derivative-grade series computes). Most of it is the closed forms of the edge and vertex distances over the face parts near input edges (the near-parallel series); the labelling is 6-7 us. The cube outward has no region overlaps on its offset side: no cell is flagged and no D_t is evaluated. "exact_swept" (2026-10-22): "exact"'s energy (b(t) = J_t / target_distance; the settle test and every whole-mesh sum as under "exact"), but every operation's rule compares the AMIPS terms of the cells it changes plus the exact CHANGE of the band integral E* = int_B (d - delta) dV, which lives only where the band B changes and is integrated there by value() on small tets (TopoOffsetTetMesh, EXACT SWEPT CHANGE). A vertex moving from x0 to x1 (smoothing, the projected step, a collapse moving v1 onto v2): the sum over the faces (x, a, b) of B's boundary through the vertex (front faces, faces on the input, on the domain wall) of sign value(x0, x1, a, b), the face ordered with its normal out of B and the sign that of (x1 - x0) along that normal: a band cell moved differs from itself by one oriented tet per face through the vertex (the boundary of a 4-simplex is a 3-cycle, which integrates to 0 in R^3), and those between two band cells cancel; exact for mixed signs; a vertex on no boundary face of B: 0. A collapse changes no cell's label; it integrates its swept tets after the engine's own tests (before them, where most attempts are refused for inverting a cell, the screw piece 15's turn-1 collapse pass took 35.0 s against 3.3 s, measured on main, 2026-10-22). A swap: interior (one label over the ring) 0; a flip: the cone from a vertex over the boundary of (new band cells) - (old band cells), which for a surface flip (a,b,c) + (a,b,d) -> (a,c,d) + (b,c,d) is +/- value(a, b, c, d), one call. A split, and the split energy gate: 0. Under TetWild's rules (a TetWild pass) nothing changes: no sum rule. The smoother's search model is the function the move is judged on: the ring's AMIPS terms plus the swept change from the solve's start x0 to x (the same faces, signs and value() calls), whose gradient and Hessian are the band integral's at x by Reynolds' transport theorem over B's boundary faces through the vertex ("front_flux"'s face derivatives; defined at x0, where every swept tet is flat); where a curved bisector crosses a piece of such a face (or a face's pieces do not tile it) the derivatives at that x are "exact"'s, from the ring's band cells, and each pass logs how many derivative evaluations took them. Why: the former model, the 7-point rule of G = psi(d) grad d over the front faces, left out the jumps of G.n across the bisectors; with it (uk-sonic, screw piece 15, 8 threads, 5 turns, 2026-10-23) 10.6% of turn 2's front solves were refused after 4 halvings, and the ring max held at one vertex through turns 1-3 (7.03 / 5.96 / 5.71x against "exact"'s 8.73 / 3.20 / 2.66x). After the solve the move stands iff the ring's AMIPS change plus the exact swept change is <= 0, else the step is halved toward the start and tested again, up to 4 times, then refused (each pass logs the solves, the moves accepted at the full step and after 1-4 halvings, and the refusals). Tested (test_exact_swept): random moves of a vertex coned to a box of random band / background / input cells at the cube's corner and across the valley's bisector, the swept change against the change of the band cells' sum of value(); a collapse onto a box corner; 3-2 and 4-4 configurations with random band subsets; a surface 3-2 flip one value() call; value() over the 24 corner orders; the search model's value against the swept change bit for bit, its gradient against central differences of its value and, at the solve's start, against "exact"'s, at the cube's corner and across the valley's bisector; where a curved bisector crosses a front face, its derivatives against "exact"'s. "surface" (2026-10-27, Spencer's HackMD "Global surface integral"): NO band term; E = (w / stop_energy^3) sum_t vol AMIPS^3 + L / front_conv^2 sum over the offset faces f of O(f), L the bounding box diagonal (so both terms are volumes and both integrands are 1 at convergence), O(f) = (A_f / |S|) sum over the face's stencil points x_i (stencil_order, EXPERIMENTAL_stencil_type; the first converged runs: "fem", order 5, its points weighted by their lumped area weights) of (d(x_i) - target_distance)^2 (w = offset_amips_weight: the AMIPS term alone is weighted, so w is the ratio of the two terms; since 2026-10-28, before which the offset term was weighted 1 - w; the first converged "surface" runs on piece08 used w 100). Every rule compares the cells' sum plus the offset faces the operation changes: a collapse may not raise it (the faces through both ends before, the survivor's after), a swap must strictly lower it (a flip of the offset surface: its two faces out, two in), a split is not judged by it (since 2026-10-28 no split has an energy rule: only the length against the sizing field proposes one), a smoothing move may not raise it over the vertex's ring and faces (strictly lower for a held vertex's projected step). The front smoother minimises the AMIPS term over the ring plus the face term of the vertex's offset faces (exact gradient and Hessian). The settle test reads O*, the max over the stencil points of (d - target_distance)^2, with settle_stall_eps (see there). EXPERIMENTAL_label_cleanup's tip / at-target flips are taken iff they strictly lower the face term. "corner_bound" is the default.

EXPERIMENTAL_settle_test · string · default "stall" · one of stall, bar

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-27), 3D, EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_rule "surface" only ("bar" under another rule is refused), with EXPERIMENTAL_settle_refinement: which test decides that a turn has settled. "stall" (the default): the O* stall test, settled when O* < front_conv^2 or O*_prev - O* <= settle_stall_eps (O* - front_conv^2), O* the max over the front's stencil points of (d - target_distance)^2 (see settle_stall_eps). "bar" (Spencer: the volume rules' settle test "but with our surface integral"): settled when O_g = int over the front of (d - target_distance)^2 dS (the face term without its weight, by the faces' stencils) fell over the turn by less than front_conv^2 times the front's current area -- O_g of a front lying front_conv off the level set everywhere, as the volume rules' bar b = front_conv^2 A / (2 target_distance) is their band term's excess for such a front. A rise settles. settle_stall_eps is refused under "bar". The marking, halving and exit of a settled turn are EXPERIMENTAL_settle_mark's, unchanged.

EXPERIMENTAL_settle_mark · string · default "vertex_edge" · one of max, rms, vertex, vertex_edge, vertex_split, stencil

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-09), with EXPERIMENTAL_settle_refinement: which test marks a front face on a settled turn (the settle, the halving and the exit are unchanged). "max": the face's largest distance from the level set, max(inside_f, outside_f), exceeds front_conv (exact up to rounding, see EXPERIMENTAL_settle_refinement). "rms": the face's share of the offset term's excess exceeds the bar energy of its area. The share, to first order in d - target_distance (divergence theorem on G = (1/2)(d - delta)^2 grad d; exact for any band shape, folds included, up to the curvature and medial-axis term), is X_f = (1/2 delta) int_f (d - delta)^2 cos(theta) dA, theta the angle between the face's normal (pointing out of the band) and grad d, signed; the bar energy of the face is front_conv^2 area(f) / (2 delta). So f is marked when the mean over f of (d - delta)^2 cos(theta) exceeds front_conv^2. The mean is taken by the 3-edge-midpoint rule (weights 1/3), exact for quadratic integrands, so exact over a face whose points all have one input face's interior as nearest feature (d affine, grad d constant). Near an input edge or vertex (d curved) it is an approximation. Across a ridge of d (the medial axis, where two input faces are equally near: the inward offset of a convex edge, the outward offset of a concave one) it can miss the face's excess entirely: measured on the prism inward (2026-10-09), one face read 0.24 bar by this rule and 7.46 bars over a 91-point grid. A face along grad d (cos theta near 0) or turned back (cos theta < 0) has a share near 0 or negative and is not marked; the max test catches such a face. "vertex": a front vertex v is marked when |d(v) - target_distance| exceeds front_conv (d over all input triangles, exact at v), and its own sizing is halved; it says nothing about the points of a face between its corners. All three tests' numbers are logged on every settled turn, whichever marks (under "rms" and "vertex" the max test's outside_f is the former corner bound, see EXPERIMENTAL_settle_refinement). Tried and removed (2026-10-25, 2026-10-26): "variance" (refine a vertex only where the errors at its faces' corners and centroids vary by more than front_conv while their mean is within it) and "remainder" (halve the corners of a face whose error at its centroid differs from the mean of its corners' errors by more than front_conv). MEASURED: "variance" never refined the single-cell stage of cube_in at 0.45 (3.68 front_conv off for 40 turns); under "remainder", t100033 inward at 0.25 delta_1 (5%, 8 threads, EXPERIMENTAL_label_cleanup "one_sided_tips") did not resolve in 30 turns -- from turn 17 on, 1 or 2 vertices were over front_conv, the worst 1.06 to 1.14 front_conv short of a crease of the target, with its band and AMIPS forces equal and opposite and its sizing scalar unchanged at turns 10, 20 and 30 (the remainder test marked one face's corners elsewhere on 4 of those 14 turns) -- where "vertex" resolved the same configuration at turn 16; with the label clean-up, "vertex" resolved cube_in at 0.45 30 of 30 (5%, 8 threads). "vertex_edge" (2026-10-26, the default): "vertex", and also both ends of a front edge whose two ends are within front_conv of the level set and whose midpoint is not have their sizing halved; these marks refine only and do not hold the exit, which stays the vertex test. One [settle edge] line per settled turn. Why: such an edge spans a stretch of the level set its corners do not see, which the vertex test passes for good. MEASURED (t100033 inward at 0.5 delta_1, 10%): at 1 thread it resolved at turn 8 where "vertex" was held by a real fold to the 30-turn cap (1979 front vertices at turn 8 against 549, the halving spreading through the gradation); at 8 threads, one run each, it resolved at turn 8 in 70 s with 1934 front vertices and 52360 tets, "vertex_split" at turn 19 in 168 s with 1425 front vertices and 56687 tets, both with no real fold. Offline, the edge test flagged 0.02-6% of the front edges of final meshes (t100033 36 of 4020, t126196 18 of 5109, screw 4 of 17136) and every real-fold edge (5 of 5), most of the rest crease or sag edges with the midpoint 1.2-2 front_conv off. "vertex_split" (2026-10-26): "vertex", and also a front face whose three corners are within front_conv of the level set but one of its three edge midpoints or its centroid is not has the edge with the midpoint farthest from the level set split (no sizing change), serially, right before the first smoothing pass of the next turn, in the slot of EXPERIMENTAL_front_pocket_split (which it needs; refused otherwise) and before its pinned cells; an edge that turn's operation passes removed is skipped. The listed edges do not hold the exit, which stays the vertex test: they are split only if the run goes on, and a run that exits leaves them unsplit. MEASURED with a turn that listed edges not exiting (8 threads): at turns 14 to 17 the vertex test passed with no real fold, so the run would have exited at turn 14; the listed edges held it, and by turn 25, when it was stopped, the front had grown from 661 to 1228 vertices. One [settle split] line per settled turn and one where the edges are split. Why that slot: split at the end of the settled turn, the next turn's collapse pass undid the splits before any smoothing had moved the new vertices, restoring the geometry at no energy cost: MEASURED (t100033 inward at 0.5 delta_1, 10%, 1 thread), 12 of turn 2's 64 split vertices and 1 of turn 3's 44 were left after the next collapse pass, and the real folds went 0 at turn 5 to 12 at turn 9. Why: such a face spans a stretch of the level set its corners do not see, which the vertex test passes for good. Against "vertex_edge" (which halves the sizing instead), see there. Not gated by its energy gain: MEASURED offline on that run's final mesh, a split of any of its 40 such edges, the new vertex placed anywhere that keeps the cells valid, lowers the offset energy by at most 0.61 of the settle bar of the edge's two front faces, the real fold's edge by 0.27; in the 5% run that resolved, the fold went at the collapse the turn after the split. The face test against the edge test alone: on the final meshes of t100033 (two runs) and t126196, every such face but one (t126196, 1 of 27) has an edge midpoint over. Read only under EXPERIMENTAL_settle_refinement. "vertex_edge" is the default (2026-10-26; before it, "vertex"). "stencil" (2026-10-28, Spencer: "enforce that every stencil point is within front_conv for convergence"): a front face is marked when a point of its offset stencil (stencil_order, EXPERIMENTAL_stencil_type: the FEM stencil's points include the corners and the edges, the interior stencil's do not) lies at or beyond front_conv of the level set, (d - target_distance)^2 >= front_conv^2, or is unmeasurable -- the per-face max of the same points and values as O*, the "surface" rule's settle metric (settle_stall_eps); its three corners have their sizing halved (down to the sizing floor; a marked face with every corner at the floor is counted and warned about), and a marked face holds the exit. So the loop exits only when every stencil point of every front face is within front_conv (and, under the "surface" rule, that alone also settles the turn). No vertex or edge-midpoint test. One more field in the [settle] line's parenthesis: the stencil test's faces over and its max in bars.

EXPERIMENTAL_gap_refinement · bool · default false

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-10), 3D, needs EXPERIMENTAL_settle_refinement. On a settled turn a band cell with a front corner is also refined (its four corners' sizing halved) when md - d(centroid) > front_conv: md is the corner mean of the bounding triangle's distance (the corner bound's own min over input triangles, see EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_rule), d(centroid) the exact distance at the cell's centroid. Where d is convex on the cell (everywhere outside a convex input) the cell's true mean of d is at least d(centroid) (Jensen), so Vol (md - d(centroid)) / target_distance bounds the corner bound's gap (bound minus true integral) from above; near a concave feature it bounds nothing. The exit also needs no such cell. Why: the gap depends on the corners' positions, and the smoother descends it with the energy. On the cylinder outward (2026-10-09) every fold of the front formed in a smoothing pass by a move that lowered the corner bound while the true integral plus AMIPS rose, and in one turn-11 pass 39 of 150 sampled front moves did that. false (the default) = only the face test refines.

EXPERIMENTAL_damping · bool · default false

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-15), 3D. Damped smoothing: every local solve of every smoothing pass of the loop (front vertices and every other vertex; the loop's every stage, init_optimize's loop and pre_smooth included) may move its vertex at most EXPERIMENTAL_damping_factor (default 0.5: half) times the length of the shortest edge at the vertex (from the vertex to any vertex of its one-ring), measured from where the vertex was when the solve started. A solve that goes further is pulled back along its step to that distance before the move's accept checks (inversion, envelope containment, the energy veto), and a held surface vertex's projected candidates beyond it are refused. Never in a TetWild pass -- optimize_construction's, the final pass -- nor in the repulsion passes before the march (since 2026-10-20; before, all of them were damped too). Each damped smoothing pass logs how many accepted moves ended on the bound ([damping]). false (the default) = no bound.

EXPERIMENTAL_damping_factor · float · default 0.5 · min 0

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-15), 3D, with EXPERIMENTAL_damping. The damping bound as a factor of the shortest edge at the vertex: each smoothing solve may move its vertex at most this times the length of its shortest edge (to any vertex of its one-ring), at the positions when the solve started. Must be > 0; a value other than the default with EXPERIMENTAL_damping false is refused with an error. 0.5 (the default) = half the shortest edge, the bound EXPERIMENTAL_damping had before this key existed.

EXPERIMENTAL_settle_refinement · bool · default true

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-09), 3D. Refinement and exit wait for the front to settle, then judge every front face by its distance from the level set d = target_distance. Each turn, after the energy criterion: dE = E_prev - E, E the offset energy -- the band term of the energy (see offset_amips_weight) summed over the band cells, without the AMIPS term, which changes wherever the mesh is improved whether the front moves or not (measured 2026-10-14, serial, Geneva settings: splits raised the whole energy through its AMIPS term by 0.7-3.6 b per turn on the cube outward) -- at the end of the turn, and E_prev at the end of the previous turn (turn 1: just before its first operation group); the bar energy b = front_conv^2 * A / (2 * target_distance), A the total area of the front faces: the excess of the offset term for a front of area A lying front_conv beyond the level set (per unit area the integral of s / target_distance over s from 0 to front_conv). The turn is settled when dE < b. An unsettled turn refines nothing and does not exit: the front is still moving, and a face judged now is judged where the front passes, not where it comes to rest. On a settled turn a front face f is marked when max(inside_f, outside_f) > front_conv, with inside_f = target_distance - min over f of d (exact: the min over input triangles P of the triangle-to-triangle distance) and outside_f = (max over f of d) - target_distance, exact up to rounding (EXPERIMENTAL_settle_mark "max"): f is cut by the input's nearest-feature regions (face prisms, edge wedges, vertex cones) as the exact band integral cuts a cell (EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_rule); on a piece where one feature's distance is d, d is convex and its max is at a vertex of the piece; on a piece whose region boundaries are curved ("rule (a)") the min over its features of each one's max is used, an upper bound. The former outside_f, the min over input triangles P of the max of d_P over f's three corners, is one triangle's convex distance and overshoots by about s^2 / (2 target_distance) where f straddles a coplanar input edge by s: measured on the cube outward (settle_mark "max", exact rule), turn 28, all 8 faces it marked read 1.06-1.26 bars by it and -0.016 to +0.020 bars by the exact max; they alone blocked the exit at that turn. Under settle_mark "rms" and "vertex" outside_f is only logged and is still the former bound. Every marked face has the sizing scalar halved at its three corners (down to the sizing floor); a marked face with all three corners at the floor cannot be refined, is counted and warned about, and blocks the exit like every marked face. Exit: settled and no face marked. The run then ends as on the ordinary exit (the TetWild final pass when max AMIPS >= stop_energy), and this exit is the front half of the verdict. The energy criterion's own refinement (its refinable faces or vertices) and its exit test do not act; its turn line is still logged. One [settle] line per turn. true is the default; false = the energy criterion's refinement and exit.

EXPERIMENTAL_coarsen_guard · string · default "bar" · one of bar, no_rise

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-28), 3D, read only with coarsen_pass true (refused otherwise). What judges a coarsening collapse. "bar" (the default): the absolute bar described under coarsen_pass -- after the collapse every offset face through the survivor keeps the larger of its two cells' AMIPS / stop_energy and the root of its face measure (the face stencil's offset error in bars) at most 1 -- the front is collapsed only by length-limited passes, and coarsen_mesh() runs at the end of every TetWild pass (the optimize_construction pass and the final pass). "no_rise" (Spencer, 2026-10-28: coarsening in the final TetWild pass, "amips should reject if the max increases, offset error should reject if its sum increases"): coarsen_mesh() runs only for the final target, once the loop converges -- at the end of the final TetWild pass when that runs (max AMIPS >= stop_energy), after TetWild's bare collapse / swap sweeps, and otherwise on its own with the final pass's setup (the "final coarsening": the final envelopes, TetWild's rules, no iterations, no bare sweeps); never in the optimize_construction pass, never after a loop that did not converge. A collapse is kept only if (a tie passes) the max AMIPS over the cells it reshapes (the survivor's ring less v2's untouched cells) does not rise above the max over the collapsed vertex's old ring, and the offset faces it changes pass the offset half: the offset faces through the survivor that are new (after) against the offset faces through the edge's two ends that are gone (before), faces in both cancelling, an unmeasurable new face refusing. Under EXPERIMENTAL_settle_mark "stencil" (Spencer 2026-10-28: "so long as all stencil points are still under the tol, the collapse is fine"): the max over the after faces' stencil points (stencil_order, EXPERIMENTAL_stencil_type) of (d - target_distance)^2 is under front_conv^2, or no larger than the same max over the before faces. Otherwise: the offset face term (the stencil's integral of (d - target_distance)^2 over a face, weighted the bounding-box diagonal / front_conv_frac^2) summed over the after faces does not exceed its sum over the before faces. No AMIPS threshold: a kept collapse may leave a cell over stop_energy. The engine's no-rise test (AMIPS / stop_energy clamped at 1, over the region) then never refuses what this keeps. Front vertices are collapsed too (the bare sweeps still leave them). Logged as one [coarsening] line (accepted, refused per quantity, the max stencil-point error at the pass's start and after) beside the engine's coarsen lines.

EXPERIMENTAL_front_pocket_split · bool · default false

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-22), 3D. Keeps one invariant in the loop: no cell is PINNED when a smoothing pass starts. A pinned cell is a cell outside the input complex, band or not, whose four corners are all on the front (VertexExtra::m_is_on_offset) (since 2026-10-22 evening band cells too; before, only the cells outside the band). Right before every smoothing pass of optimize_offset_loop() (each operation group's passes, and pre_smooth's), every pinned cell has ONE of its edges split, the longest that is an edge of no live offset-surface face (edge_is_offset_surface_live() false), so the midpoint is not on the front and every cell around it has a corner that is not; the split is the loop's own (split_edge(): labels, tags, sizing and rests as in the split pass), and when it is refused the next longest such edge is tried. A pinned cell with no such edge (all six on the offset surface) has instead the longest edge of one of its faces that is not an offset face split (that face's edges are all on the offset surface): the split makes an edge from the midpoint to the face's third corner that is off the offset surface, in both of the cell's children, and the next round splits it -- a vertex off the front on that face, a corner of all four of the cell's descendants (simplicial_embedding()'s face split, made of two of the loop's edge splits). MEASURED before (cube_in, target 0.3): every such cell had exactly three faces on the offset surface and stood alone under a front vertex of valence 3. A pinned cell with all four faces on the offset surface (a one-cell component of its label) is not split and is counted. The scan is repeated until it finds no pinned cell with an edge to split, at most 10 rounds (a warning when the cap stops it); one [pocket split] line per application gives the pinned cells found and how many of them have all six edges (all four faces) on the offset surface, the edges split, the rounds, the pinned cells left (all six edges on the offset surface, or an edge off it with every split refused), and how many of the pinned cells found are BAND cells (all four corners on the front, inside the band). Why: only smoothing moves vertices, and no vertex joins or leaves the front during a smoothing pass, so a cell can only be flattened during smoothing, and only from a cell that is pinned when the pass starts. The band term depends only on the band as a region (under the exact rule, the integral of (d - target_distance) / target_distance over the band), so a vertex off the front does not change it (a vertex on the input complex carries no band term): the AMIPS term alone moves such a vertex, and it keeps the vertex's cells shaped. A pinned cell has no such corner: the band term pulls all four onto the level set d = target_distance, so the level set fixes its shape -- a sliver (relative volume of the order of curvature x edge length) -- and where the level set curves the wrong way the energy flattens it to zero volume, a fold of the front. Hence the invariant. A split of an edge off the front makes no pinned cell (every cell it makes has the midpoint, off the front, as a corner) and removes at least one. MEASURED 2026-10-22 on cube_in at target 0.3 (serial, 7 turns): the outside-the-band version converged in 5 turns with no fold against 7 unconverged turns and 104 folded faces. MEASURED 2026-10-23 on a 20-case suite (EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_rule "exact", 4 threads, max_rounds 15; this key before the six-edge split was added), a fold being an edge of two front faces whose normals out of the band are within 30 degrees of opposite, and a fold on a pinned cell one whose two faces are faces of one flattened cell: off, 18 of 20 cases resolved; on, 20 of 20, and no fold on a pinned cell at the last turn. cube_in at target 0.3: not resolved in 15 turns, 174 folds (152 on a pinned cell) -> resolved at turn 3, no fold. Screw piece 15 at target 0.12: not resolved in 15 turns, 291 folds (270 on a pinned cell) -> resolved at turn 4, no fold. The six-edge split, MEASURED on cube_in at target 0.3 (serial, 7 turns): 18 pinned cells with all six edges on the offset surface found over the passes, all split within 2 rounds, none left; resolved at turn 5. The group is then run as its operation passes and one call per smoothing pass (as repulsion_rounds runs its groups), because the engine gives no point between a group's operation pass and its first smoothing pass, nor between two of its smoothing passes; besides the splits, the rounding sweep then runs after every smoothing pass instead of after the group's last, and each pass logs its own energy and time lines. Not in a TetWild pass, not before the march. false (the default): nothing.

EXPERIMENTAL_front_spanned_split · bool · default false

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-24), 3D, needs EXPERIMENTAL_front_pocket_split. Extends its invariant from cells to every simplex: no SPANNED simplex when a smoothing pass starts. A spanned simplex is an edge, face or cell outside the input complex that is on no offset-surface face (an edge on none, a face not one) while all its corners are on the front; a pinned cell is the spanned cell. Every cell around a spanned edge or face has one label, so the simplex lies inside that label's region, and where the level set is flat the front is a plane through its corners: a cell on it between it and the front has height at most twice the front's distance to the level set, so the band term flattens it as the front converges, though every such cell may have a corner off the front. In each round of front_pocket_split(), before the pinned cells: every spanned edge is split (its midpoint is off the front, a corner of every cell made); then every spanned face whose three edges are on the offset surface has its longest edge split, and the next round splits the edge from that midpoint to the face's third corner (the pinned cell's six-edge split). Lowest dimension first, so a face or cell is split only when no spanned simplex of lower dimension lies on it. Counted in the [pocket split] line as spanned edges / faces found and split. MEASURED before this (cube_in at target 0.45, 1% tolerance, the pocket split on, 1 thread, 40 turns): spanned edges and faces stay through the run (e.g. turn 16 after smoothing: 12 edges, 40 faces, 0 cells); cells on them have median h/l 0.02 to 0.05 against 0.28 to 0.39 for the other cells at the front (turns 9 to 37). false (the default): nothing.

EXPERIMENTAL_exit_no_folds · bool · default false

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-26; foldover faces only since 2026-10-27), 3D. The loop does not exit on a turn whose front has a real fold with a foldover face. A real fold: an offset-surface edge with exactly two offset faces whose normals out of the band are within 30 degrees of opposite (count_real_folds(), the fold work's definition of 2026-10-24: the edge of a zero-volume sheet). A foldover face: one whose normal, out of the band, is more than foldover_angle from the field's normal, grad d at its centroid (front_face_field_angle(), the debug frames' field_normal_angle); a face that cannot be measured counts as one. The exit test is otherwise unchanged; a held turn continues the loop. One [exit folds] line per turn gives the count of real folds, and one [exit folds foldover] line per turn with a fold the folds with a foldover face and the largest angle of their faces, with the key on or off. Why: the vertex exit tests only the front's vertices, and a flat sheet of inner cells lying within front_conv of the level set passes it. Measured (cube_in at 0.45, front_conv 5%, 30 runs, 8 threads): one run exited with an inner region of 0.5% of the target's volume, every front point within 0.76 front_conv, 5 real folds; 5-7 of each batch's 28-30 exits had 1-5 real folds. Why only the folds with a foldover face: where the level set itself has a ridge sharper than 30 degrees, the correct front is a fold whose faces follow the field, and holding the exit for every real fold (the key until 2026-10-27) held such runs to the turn cap. MEASURED offline (every turn of the 10-26 batch held for the folds: 117 turns of 31 runs, d exact): in the 4 runs held to the 30-turn cap (p70565 piece17 and input1, inward at 0.5 and 0.25 delta_1, 10%), 845 of 858 folds had both faces within 10 degrees of the field, on a level set 7.7 to 27 degrees sharp there (piece17's input has convex edges of 26.1 and 27.0 degrees; input1 a part just over 2 delta thick); the other 13, at 87 to 131 degrees, were at 2 early turns. In the 27 runs that resolved, every one of the 74 folds of their 32 held turns had a face 32 to 161 degrees from the field (median 108), though 73 had every corner, edge midpoint and centroid of both faces within front_conv of the level set: a test of the faces' distance instead would have let 31 of those 32 turns exit. The margin is thin on that side: the nearest such fold, 32.1 degrees (screw15 inward at 0.25 delta_1). MEASURED with this rule (those 31 runs, 8 threads): all 31 resolved; the 4 in 38 turns against 120 at the cap, each releasing once, 35 folds whose faces lay within 0.57 front_conv of the level set, within 13.1 degrees of the field, on a level set 7.7 to 31.4 degrees sharp there; the 27 released none and exited with no fold. false (the default): the exit test alone; the counts are still logged.

EXPERIMENTAL_label_cleanup · string · default "off" · one of off, one_sided, one_sided_tips, one_sided_at_target, energy_decrease

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-26), 3D, with EXPERIMENTAL_front_pocket_split true (refused otherwise). The one exception to cell labels being fixed after construction. In every operation group of the loop (once per turn with interleaved_smoothing false), after its operation passes (split, collapse, swap) and before the condition-1 splits that precede its first smoothing pass, a cell on the band / non-band interface (a candidate: a cell with a face shared with a cell of the other label, neither of them the input complex) whose own geometry puts it on the other side of the level set d = target_distance takes the other label, where that keeps the topology of both. Why there: a flip with f = 1 or 2 (below) leaves the cell with all four corners on the front, a pinned cell, which those splits handle, and one with f = 3 removes a pinned cell; the smoothing pass then moves the new front in the same turn. The side test: "one_sided" (conservative): non-band -> band iff U(t) < target_distance, U the min over input triangles of the max of their distance over t's corners, an upper bound of d on t; band -> non-band iff d(c) - max_k |v_k - c| > target_distance, c the centroid, a lower bound of d on t (d is 1-Lipschitz). It reads d through the exact band integral, built under EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_rule "exact" or "front_flux", EXPERIMENTAL_settle_mark "max" or DEBUG_output; otherwise it throws. Eligible cells only: every cell sharing a vertex with t is band or non-band, not plastic (use_rest_pose makes every non-band cell plastic, and with it the clean-up flips nothing), and of the one tag of its label there; no corner of t is on the input complex, on another tracked surface (a tag boundary, the box) or on the mesh boundary. The topology test, f = the faces of t shared with a cell of the other label: f = 0 refused (a new piece, or the front pinched at an edge or vertex); f = 1 refused if the corner opposite that face is in a cell of the other label; f = 2 refused if the edge on neither face is in a cell of the other label; f = 3 allowed (the fourth face becomes front); f = 4 refused (t is a whole piece; the flip deletes it). The other label then meets t in exactly its f faces, a disk. Serial passes over the candidates in tid order, each reading the labels as the flips before it left them, repeated until a pass flips nothing. They end: no vertex moves and a cell's side test reads its own corners alone, so a cell flips at most once (a second flip throws). After the flips, everything derived from the labels is re-derived where it changed: the closed labels and the cached front class of the flipped cells' faces, edges and corners, the corners' front flags and vertex order, the band-region map. One [label cleanup] line: passes; flips each way; what the last pass left (candidates, cells on the other side by the side test, of them skipped for eligibility and refused by topology per f); E before and after; the components (face adjacency) of the band and of the non-band region before and after, where a change throws; the front edges on more than two front faces before and after. MEASURED before the key (cube_in at target 0.45, 5% tolerance, 30-run batches): some runs end with thin non-band cells left beyond the level set, one with 117 cells reaching 5.6 tolerances out, where E is 1.2e-7 above its optimum against a settle bar of 3.5e-5, so nothing removes them. "off" (the default): nothing changes. "one_sided_tips" (2026-10-26): "one_sided", and also a cell with three faces on the other label whose four corners are all within front_conv of the level set flips iff that strictly lowers E: non-band -> band iff its band term (EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_rule) is < 0, band -> non-band iff it is > 0 (the AMIPS term of a cell that is not plastic does not read its label, so a flip changes E by exactly the band term). Why: under "one_sided" 9 of 30 runs exited with a real fold, a blade of flat non-band cells reaching up to 0.07 front_conv into the target; a blade that no collapse, swap or smoothing removes is, when the operation passes end, one such cell (cube_in at 0.45, 5%). "one_sided_at_target" (2026-10-26): "one_sided", and also any cell with a front face (1, 2 or 3 faces on the other label) whose four corners are all within front_conv of the level set flips iff that strictly lowers E, by the sign of its band term: the tip rule of "one_sided_tips" without its three-face condition. Why: in t126196 inward at 0.5 delta_1 (10%, 8 threads, "one_sided_tips") the run hit the 30-turn cap held by 3 real folds; from turn 4 on, the band cells carrying the folds' faces after the clean-up had all four corners within front_conv and a positive band term, all with two faces on the other label (one with one, at turn 25), which the tip rule refuses; at turn 30 the one-sided test read 14 to 16 front_conv short and the topology test allowed both cells. Removed 2026-10-26: "energy" (every candidate flipped by the sign of its band term alone). MEASURED (cube_in at 0.45, 5%, 30 runs, 8 threads, damping off): 23 of 30 resolved, every failure the non-band region reduced to one flat cell covering none of the target. "energy_decrease" (2026-10-28, Spencer; EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_rule "surface" only, refused otherwise): no side test and no corner gate -- every cell with a front face whose flip strictly lowers the "surface" rule's face term over its four faces (a face shared with a cell of its own label becomes a front face, one shared with the other label stops being one; the flip changes E by exactly that, an eligible cell being not plastic) flips, if eligible and allowed by the topology test, the same tests as the other modes. A cell may flip again in a later pass (every flip strictly lowers E, so the passes end; at most 100 passes, with a warning).

docs.title: Testing options
docs.text:
For the test suites. (1)

TESTING_allow_mult_comp · bool · default false

TESTING (2026-10-16), 3D. true = an input complex of more than one connected piece (connected components under vertex connectivity; the count is logged as 'Input complex: N connected piece(s)') is accepted. false (the default) = such an input is refused with an error when the offset potential is built, after the construction and before the optimization; with optimize_offset false no potential is built and nothing is refused. Accepted, the energy's band term (every EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_rule) reads the distance to all the input's triangles, every piece at once, as it does for one piece, and a warning is logged.

docs.title: Tracking (tracking)
docs.text:
Rebuilds the map between an application's input surface and its output from the history the application recorded (history_output): one bijective local map per operation, composed in order. operation selects what to do with it: report on it (info), map points (map), carry fields (transfer), follow feature points (features), or do the same through a tet mesh's volume (volume, map_volume).

Tutorial · Spec source · Defaults · JSON Schema

docs.title: application
docs.text:
string · required · one of tracking

Application name must be tracking.

docs.title: history
docs.text:
string · required

A history, recorded by an application's history_output, from which the map is rebuilt: a surface's (isotropic_remeshing, qslim, shortest_edge_collapse, tetwild, simwild) or curves' (triwild); the history says which. On the file route the file it wrote, on the memory route the bytes it returned in its report as history (a JSON binary value, bytes in Python; wm.read_history reads them from a file). The memory route never takes a file name here.

docs.title: operation
docs.text:
string · default "info" · one of info, transfer, map, features, volume, map_volume

info: build the map and report what it holds, where it stops being a bijection, and how far the output's face centroids (segment midpoints, for curves) move when mapped to the input and back. transfer (surfaces): carry every field of input's triangles onto the output surface and write it to output (on the memory route: return it as mesh). map: map the points of the file points to the output (direction to_output) or back to the input (to_input), and write them to output_points; file route only. features (curves): write the input's feature points -- curve ends, junctions, input points -- to output_points, one input_vertex output_vertex per line: a vertex of the input files (the curve files' vertices, in order, then the point files', from 0) and the output vertex it ended at, -1 for none; on the memory route the report holds them instead, as feature_points, a list of such pairs. volume (tet meshes): build the map of the volume from volume_history, and check it on samples points near the tracked surface of tet_mesh (the mesh the volume history starts from: <output>_history_input.msh, the output mesh history_input on the memory route): how far they move, the map's conformal distortion and Jacobian there, whether they end in the same region of output_tet_mesh (the mesh it ends at: simwild's <output>.msh, tetwild's <output>_history_output.msh -- on the memory route the output meshes mesh and history_output), and how close the inverse brings them back; the report holds what it finds. Without tet_mesh, every operation's map is built. map_volume: map the points of points through the volume, to the output (direction to_output) or back (to_input), and write them to output_points: x y z per line, written back with the tags of their region; or tet b0 b1 b2 b3, a tet of tet_mesh (to_output) or output_tet_mesh (to_input) -- a row of the file's tets, as io::read_mesh (wm.read_mesh) gives them -- and barycentric coordinates in its corners' order, written back as a tet of the other mesh, of the point's own region, -1 for none; file route only.

docs.title: input
docs.text:
string · default ""

transfer: the surface the history starts from -- the same triangles in the same order: a gmsh file, as io::read_mesh (wm.read_mesh) reads it, whose triangle fields are carried onto the output -- per face (labels), or per corner (uv and normal, three values per corner, corner after corner: texture coordinates) -- or a triangle mesh of another format, as read, with none. Empty: the input files of the application that recorded the history, from its parameters -- refused for a history recorded on the memory route, whose input was a mesh. Every output face gets input_face too, the input face its centroid maps to. On the memory route: the key of the mesh the history starts from, which a transfer needs; the output surface is returned as mesh.

docs.title: output
docs.text:
string · default "out.msh"

transfer: the output surface, written as a gmsh file through io::write_mesh, the carried fields as attributes of its triangles: what wm.read_mesh reads.

docs.title: points
docs.text:
string · default ""

map: a text file of points, one per line, numbers separated by blanks, '#' starting a comment. On the input (direction to_output): face b0 b1 b2, a triangle of the input files -- the triangles of all of them, in order, as the files hold them, from 0 -- and barycentric coordinates with respect to its corners in file order; for a history that starts at a tet mesh's tracked surface (simwild on a .msh input), v0 v1 v2 b0 b1 b2, three vertices of the tet mesh the history starts from (<output>_history_input.msh) at the corners of a tracked face, in any order, with barycentric coordinates in that order. On the output (direction to_input): face b0 b1 b2, a triangle of the output file, for an application whose output is a surface (isotropic_remeshing); v0 v1 v2 b0 b1 b2, three vertices of the output tet mesh at the corners of a tracked face, in any order, with barycentric coordinates in that order, for one whose output is a tet mesh (tetwild, simwild). On curves (triwild): segment b0 b1 on the input, a segment of the input curve files -- the segments of all of them, in order, a polyline's consecutive vertex pairs, from 0 -- with barycentric coordinates with respect to its ends in file order; v0 v1 b0 b1 on the output, two vertices of the output mesh at the ends of a tracked edge, in either order, with barycentric coordinates in that order.

docs.title: output_points
docs.text:
string · default ""

map: where to write the mapped points, one line per point of points, in the same order, as described for points on the side they are mapped to, relative to input_dir as points is. A point with no image has the id -1. features: where to write the feature points, relative to input_dir too.

docs.title: direction
docs.text:
string · default "to_output" · one of to_output, to_input

map: to_output maps points on the input to the output; to_input maps points on the output back to the input, the inverse map.

docs.title: tet_mesh
docs.text:
string · default ""

transfer: the tet mesh (gmsh) the history's application wrote, whose tracked surface is where the history ends. With output_tet_mesh, the fields are written onto it: a copy of it, with the tracked surface as rows of its triangle block, on its own vertices by the ids the history saved, carrying the fields. A tracked face the block has already (a face tag of simwild's) takes the fields on its row; the others are rows added after them. A row that is no tracked face gets 0, and input_face -1. volume: the tet mesh the volume history starts from, sampled near its tracked surface; on the memory route the key of a mesh given.

docs.title: uv_field
docs.text:
string · default "uv"

transfer: the per-corner field output_obj takes its texture coordinates from (the first two values of each corner).

docs.title: output_obj
docs.text:
string · default ""

transfer: also write the output as a textured Wavefront OBJ, with uv_field as its texture coordinates and a material mapping texture. Empty: not written. Not on the memory route, which writes no files.

docs.title: texture
docs.text:
string · default "checker.png"

transfer: the image the material of output_obj maps.

docs.title: output_tet_mesh
docs.text:
string · default ""

transfer: where to write tet_mesh with the fields on its tracked surface. On the memory route tet_mesh is the key of a mesh, and the result is returned as tet_mesh; nothing is written. volume: the tet mesh the volume history ends at, which each sampled point is checked to end in its region of; on the memory route the key of a mesh given.

docs.title: smoothing
docs.text:
string · default "flatten" · one of flatten, barycentric

How the map follows a vertex smoothing step. flatten: the vertex's star before and after the move is flattened jointly, so points stay where they were on the surface, at one SLIM solve per move; on curves, points keep their place along the curve, by arc length. barycentric: points keep their face (segment) and barycentric coordinates, riding along with the vertex by at most its step, at no cost, as BijectiveRemesh does.

docs.title: scaffold
docs.text:
string · default "box" · one of box, ring

The scaffold of each local map's joint flattening, which keeps the outline the two patches share a simple polygon while SLIM lowers their distortion. box: the region between the outline and a box three times the patch, triangulated anew before every iteration, as in BijectiveRemesh; it follows the patch wherever the flattening takes it. ring: one ring of triangles out to a fixed copy of the outline; about 2.4 times faster, but it pulls the outline back and keeps it from stretching, so local maps are more distorted.

docs.title: collapse_patch
docs.text:
string · default "both_stars" · one of both_stars, removed_star

The faces each collapse's local map flattens. both_stars: the stars of both ends of the edge before, onto the survivor's star after; the least distorted surface map. removed_star: the removed vertex's star before, onto the faces it becomes, with the survivor on the outline: more distorted on the surface, but it changes only the faces the collapse changes, which is what a map of the volume around the surface needs. Where those faces after are not a disk on the same outline (a vertex of the boundary or a curve collapsed into one off it), both stars.

docs.title: volume_history
docs.text:
string · default ""

volume, map_volume: the volume history (an application's volume_history_output) recorded with history, the surface history. On the file route the file it wrote, on the memory route the bytes it returned in its report as volume_history (a JSON binary value, bytes in Python; wm.read_history reads them from a file).

docs.title: samples
docs.text:
int · default 1000

volume: how many points to sample near the tracked surface of tet_mesh.

docs.title: input_dir
docs.text:
string · default ""

Directory where the input files are located. This is injected by the application and should not be set by the user.

docs.title: log_file
docs.text:
string · default ""

Logs are not just printed on the terminal but also saved in this file.

docs.title: TriWild (triwild)
docs.text:
Triangulates the plane around curve networks as they come -- polylines that cross, overlap or leave gaps -- following TriWild: the curves are simplified within the envelope, embedded exactly into a triangle mesh around them, and the mesh is then optimized for quality while the embedded curves stay inside an envelope around the input. filter removes the triangles outside.

Tutorial · Spec source · Defaults · JSON Schema

Cite: Hu et al. 2019, TriWild: Robust Triangulation with Curve Constraints

docs.title: application
docs.text:
string · required · one of triwild

Application name must be triwild.

docs.title: input
docs.text:
list of string · required · min 1

List of input curve networks: OBJ files of polylines ('v' and 'l' lines).

Each entry: One curve network: an OBJ file of polylines ('v' and 'l' lines).

docs.title: input_names
docs.text:
list of string · default []

List of names for the input meshes. If no names are assigned, the meshes will be named tag_0, tag_1, etc.

Each entry: Name for one input mesh.

docs.title: output
docs.text:
string · default "out"

Output file name (without extension).

docs.title: eps_rel
docs.text:
float · default 0.001

Envelope thickness relative to the bounding box diagonal.

docs.title: length_rel
docs.text:
float · default 0.05

Target edge length relative to the bounding box diagonal.

docs.title: stop_energy
docs.text:
float · default 100

Target energy. If all triangles have an energy below this, triwild will stop. Held numerically equal to tetwild's for parity, but note the two numbers are not the same quantity: this is the raw AMIPS2D energy, whose floor (an equilateral triangle) is 2, while tetwild compares the cube root of AMIPS3D, whose floor is 3. So 100 is 50x the floor here against ~33x there, i.e. a looser target in 2D than the same number buys in 3D. Making the two comparable would mean normalizing both energies by their dimension, which would change every logged figure and break comparison with existing runs; parity of the knob was chosen over parity of the target. At 100 a 300-model trial finished with a median max energy of 88.9 and a median iteration count of 1, i.e. one pass and stop; the 19686-model sweep converged 100% with a median max energy of 19.8 because most of it ran at the older target of 20.

docs.title: filter
docs.text:
string · default "none" · one of flood, input, tracked, none

Remove the outside region based on different criteria. 'flood': flood fill; the region that dominates the mesh boundary is dropped. 'input': winding number w.r.t. the inputs; faces inside no input are dropped. 'tracked': winding number w.r.t. the tracked curves, oriented as the input was -- the curves the mesh conforms to rather than the input, all inputs at once (coincident curves add up, opposite ones cancel); faces at most 1/2 are dropped. 'none': Do not filter. All three filters need closed input curves -- on an open polyline 'inside' is not defined and the result is arbitrary.

docs.title: input_points
docs.text:
list of string · default []

List of input POINT files: every vertex of each file is a feature point to preserve, whether or not the file also has edges (they are ignored). Each point is inserted as a vertex of the triangulation and anchored like a polyline endpoint: some output vertex stays within eps of it, collapses that would break that are refused, and smoothing may move the carrying vertex only within the eps ball. Free points can also be supplied inline: a vertex of an /input curve file with no incident edge is anchored the same way. A point lying in a region the /filter discards leaves the triangle mesh with that region, but survives in the <output>_features.obj feature output, and DEBUG_feature_retention reports the PRE-filter state -- a feature preserved through the optimization is never reported lost because extraction discarded its region.

Each entry: One input point file (any edge-mesh format; only the vertices are used).

docs.title: preserve_feature_points
docs.text:
bool · default true

Keep the curve network's 0-dimensional features -- the endpoints of open polylines, and junctions -- within eps of where the arrangement placed them. Each such vertex is bound to a specific feature point, so a collapse is refused when it would leave that point unrepresented or move it further than eps, and smoothing may move the vertex anywhere inside that ball but no further. Without this the collapse pass deletes open polylines outright: a polyline erodes into its own tip until a single segment is left, and that segment carries a feature at BOTH ends, which the surface order test does not refuse (it only forbids collapsing a feature into a non-feature). Measured on the 2D dataset, model 215292 went from 28 open components after the arrangement to 0 in the output. Turn off only to reproduce the old behaviour.

docs.title: preserve_topology
docs.text:
bool · default false

Preserve the topology of the input curve network. This forces remove_duplicate_eps to merge only exactly coincident vertices, stops the input simplification from merging two junctions or endpoints, and enables the substructure link condition during optimization. When unset, all three are relaxed and the topology may change.

docs.title: max_iterations
docs.text:
int · default 80

Maximum iterations before stopping.

docs.title: skip_simplify
docs.text:
bool · default false

If true, input simplification will be skipped. The input curves are otherwise coarsened first, by collapsing their shortest segments while staying inside the simplification envelope, so the exact arrangement and the initial mesh do not carry input detail far below the target edge length.

docs.title: simplify_envelope_ratio
docs.text:
float · default 0.5

Envelope thickness used for the input simplification, as a fraction of the one used for the triangulation. Simplifying inside a tighter envelope reserves the remainder as headroom: if the simplification is allowed to place vertices at the full limit, the optimizer starts with a mesh where almost every move already lies outside and most operations are vetoed. 1.0 restores the old behaviour of sharing a single envelope.

docs.title: optimize_envelope_around_simplified
docs.text:
bool · default false

Build the optimizer's envelope around the SIMPLIFIED geometry at the remaining tolerance (eps - simplify_eps) instead of around the original input at the full eps. The deviation budget is identical by the triangle inequality, but the geometry starts at the CENTRE of the envelope it is judged against rather than somewhere inside it. The envelope is a hard veto rather than a penalty, so a mesh handed over close to the boundary has most of its moves refused. Costs elements: holding the surface within eps/2 of the simplified geometry is stricter than eps of the input wherever simplification smoothed detail away, measured at 2-3x the output tets on tetwild at unchanged final quality. Off by default.

docs.title: simplify_use_sample_envelope
docs.text:
bool · default false

Use the sampled envelope instead of the exact one for the input simplification only; the triangulation keeps whatever use_sample_envelope selects. Off by default, like use_sample_envelope; the opt-in buys speed, since the exact envelope dominates the cost of simplifying a large curve network. Both backends guarantee the same thing, that everything they accept lies within simplify_envelope_ratio * eps of the input; they differ only in how much of that budget they manage to use, so this does not change what simplify_envelope_ratio means.

docs.title: use_sample_envelope
docs.text:
bool · default false

Use the sampled envelope instead of the exact one. Both describe the same envelope -- the eps-neighbourhood of the input -- and both are given the same eps; neither is wider than the other. They differ in how much of that eps they can use. The sampled test places points along a query and asks whether each is within some radius of the input; since it cannot see what happens between two samples, it shrinks that radius to stay conservative, and so rejects some geometry that is genuinely inside. The exact one decides coverage by the union of the input's eps-neighbourhoods directly and spends almost nothing on conservatism. The difference that matters in practice: a segment bridging a gap between two input curves is rejected by the exact envelope and accepted by the sampled one whenever the gap falls between samples.

docs.title: skip_winding_number
docs.text:
bool · default false

Skip the finalize-phase winding numbers of the inputs. They are needed to filter the outside region (filter != 'none') and to tag the faces per input, which is what the MSH groups are built from -- so skipping them also empties the output groups. Ignored (with a warning) when filter != 'none', which requires them.

docs.title: compute_flood_fill
docs.text:
bool · default false

Compute the flood-fill parts -- the regions the tracked curves separate -- and write them (the VTU field flood_fill) even when filter is not 'flood', which computes them anyway. A serial pass over every face; left out of the output otherwise.

docs.title: remove_duplicate_eps
docs.text:
float · default 0

Merge vertices in the input meshes that are closer than this fraction of the bounding box diagonal, dropping the edges that become degenerate or duplicated. This is applied to each input mesh separately. 0 merges only exactly coincident vertices, which is still needed to build the segment connectivity; negative skips the pass entirely. Ignored when preserve_topology is set: merging vertices that are merely close welds curves together and so removes loops and junctions, therefore only exactly coincident vertices are merged in that case.

docs.title: split_high_valence_threshold
docs.text:
int · default 0

Incident-triangle count above which a vertex accepts only one valence-increasing split per split pass, or 0 to disable. A well-shaped triangle mesh has vertex valence around 6; a split cascade can drive one vertex much higher, at which point every operation touching it is O(valence) and the pass stalls. Splitting an edge leaves its endpoints' counts unchanged and adds one to each vertex opposite the edge, so the gate applies to those. Expect this to fire far less often than in 3D, where the edge's link is a whole ring rather than one or two vertices.

docs.title: project_line_search_steps
docs.text:
int · default 12

Bisections tried by the projected line search before it gives up on a vertex: the step along the Newton direction is halved this many times, each candidate projected onto the input, and the first that does not invert and lowers the worst incident element is taken.

docs.title: project_line_search_nested_steps
docs.text:
int · default 0

After the projected line search gives up, revisit each candidate and bisect between the interpolated point and its projection this many times, taking the longest step toward the input that still does not invert and still lowers the worst element. Lets a vertex whose one-ring cannot tolerate a full projection still travel toward the input, instead of being refused every pass from the same place. 0 disables the pass.

docs.title: smoothing_mode
docs.text:
string · default "projected" · one of projected, exact

How smoothing places a surface vertex. 'projected': smooth with AMIPS alone as if interior, then walk back toward the start projecting each candidate onto the input; accept the first projected candidate that does not invert and strictly lowers the worst incident element, else do not move. Lands exactly on the input; no weights. 'exact': minimize w_amips * AMIPS + (1-w_amips) * (d/eps)^2 with the true region-wise Hessian of the distance to the piecewise-linear input; sliding is free where the input is flat, held at corners, constrained along 3D edges and curve segments. Rests a w_amips-proportional distance off the input.

docs.title: w_amips
docs.text:
float · default 0.0001

Relative weight of the AMIPS quality term against the envelope term during smoothing; the envelope weight is 1 - w_amips. The small default makes smoothing primarily about staying on the input curves, with quality as a secondary preference.

docs.title: num_smoothing_passes
docs.text:
int · default 2

Number of smoothing passes per optimization iteration. Smoothing is the only phase that improves quality without changing connectivity, so when split, collapse and swap have run out of useful moves it is the only thing that can still lower the energy. Was 10; lowered to 2 once surface vertices stopped being skipped by skip_good_regions, which made each pass do real work -- on Thingi10K 240280 a pass costs 41-51s and moves fewer vertices each time (accepted 18606 -> 17077 over five passes, envelope rejections 11316 -> 12237), so the later passes in a run of 10 buy very little for their cost.

docs.title: interleaved_smoothing
docs.text:
bool · default true

Interleave smoothing between the topology passes: split + smoothing, collapse + smoothing, swaps + smoothing, instead of split, collapse, swaps followed by num_smoothing_passes smoothing passes. On by default in triwild: per iteration it reaches a given energy sooner than the batched schedule (on 122839, 102 vs 535 at iteration 5 and 25 vs 69 at iteration 13), at the cost of roughly 3x the work per iteration since each topology pass gets its own smoothing. tetwild still defaults to off, pending the same measurement there.

docs.title: interleaved_smoothing_passes
docs.text:
int · default 1

Smoothing passes to run after each topology pass when interleaved_smoothing is set. One is enough with interleaving on, since there are three of them per iteration.

docs.title: colored_smoothing
docs.text:
bool · default true

Parallel smoothing (num_threads > 0) by color class: the vertices are split into classes of pairwise non-adjacent vertices, smoothed one class after another, each class fully in parallel without locks. The result does not depend on the number of threads. false: the locked, partitioned smoothing pass, whose result depends on the thread schedule. Serial runs (num_threads 0) are the same either way.

docs.title: allow_junction_cleanup
docs.text:
bool · default true

Let the operations clean up junctions, anchoring only the endpoints of open polylines. The erosion the endpoint guard exists for is a property of ENDPOINTS -- a polyline eats its own tip -- and does not apply to a junction (valence >= 3 in the constrained edges), because every curve through a junction remains a constrained edge and the envelope still holds it within eps. Anchoring junctions costs most on a self-intersecting input, where nearly every arrangement vertex is a crossing: on model 242427, 79615 of 87610 vertices are junctions, so almost every edge joins two of them and collapse is refused there. When this option was added (August 2026) that model never left MAX_ENERGY with junctions anchored. It now converges either way, but anchored it keeps 2.6 times the vertices: at stop_energy 10, max energy 9.98 with 5476 output vertices in 14 s with junctions free, and 14257 in 19 s anchored (8 threads, October 2026). The two models the endpoint guard was introduced for (215292, 134005) were bit-identical either way in August. Ignored when preserve_feature_points is off. Defaults to false when history_output is set and preserve_feature_points is on: a junction the operations slide along a curve drags the curve map with it, stretched by large factors (on model 190246 a junction slid 14 units in one smoothing step, and points there came back 6.76 away from where they started).

docs.title: history_output
docs.text:
string · default ""

Record every change to the tracked curves, from the input files as read to the output, and save the history here (see wmtk/history): the tracking component rebuilds the map between the two from it. The output names a point on its curves by two vertices of the output mesh. A filter's removal of tracked edges is recorded too, as segments no map can follow. Anchors junctions unless allow_junction_cleanup is given or preserve_feature_points is off, so the output differs from a run without recording; give allow_junction_cleanup to get the same output with and without. On the memory route no file is written: any non-empty value records the history, and the bytes of the file it would be are returned in the report as history (bytes in Python; history::write_history or wm.write_history saves them). Empty: no recording.

docs.title: write_vtu
docs.text:
bool · default true

Write not just MSH but also VTU output.

docs.title: preallocation_factor
docs.text:
float · default 6.0 · min 1.0

Mesh storage (connectivity + attributes) is preallocated to this factor times the live element count at init and consolidation. Operations take fresh slots from that headroom and are retried once it is exhausted. Lower it for pure-decimation runs, raise it for aggressive refinement.

docs.title: max_expected_iterations
docs.text:
int · default 0

Fail the run if mesh_improvement needed more than this many iterations, even if it did reach stop_energy. 0 disables the check. This is a regression guard rather than a quality target: an input that normally converges in a handful of iterations and suddenly needs the whole budget means the sizing-refinement trigger stopped firing when it should, which is a silent slowdown that no energy or envelope assertion catches.

docs.title: stuck_refine_stall_eps
docs.text:
float · default 0.1

Refine when the last iteration's improvement was at most this fraction of the distance the max energy still has to cover: (prev_max - max) <= eps * (max - stop_energy). Equivalently, refine unless the mesh is on course to reach the target within about 1/eps more iterations. 0 => only when it does not improve at all.

docs.title: stuck_refine_cooldown
docs.text:
int · default 1

After a refinement, skip this many improvement iterations before refining again (let the operations act on the new sizing field). 1 by default: refining every iteration can outrun the operations entirely -- on triwild20k 189017 at eps_rel 1e-4 the mesh runs away to 5.8M faces and never converges at 0, and converges at 9.9994 in 35 iterations at 1. Costs ~5% iterations across the challenging models at no wall-time cost.

docs.title: stuck_refine_num_worst
docs.text:
int · default 0 · min 0

Number of worst triangles whose neighborhoods are refined when stuck. 0 => refine all triangles with energy above the filter_energy, which is max(max_energy / 100, stop_energy). Note that the AMIPS2D energy of an equilateral triangle is 2, so with a small stop_energy the filter catches nearly the whole mesh; set this to a positive value there.

docs.title: stuck_refine_rings
docs.text:
int · default 0 · min 0

Graph rings around each worst triangle included in the stuck refinement. 0 => only the worst triangle itself, 1 => its neighbors, 2 => neighbors of neighbors, etc.

docs.title: stuck_refine_factor
docs.text:
float · default 0.5

Multiplicative reduction of the sizing scalar per stuck refinement (0.5 => halve).

docs.title: stuck_refine_min_scalar
docs.text:
float · default 0.001

Lower bound on the sizing scalar during stuck refinement.

docs.title: stuck_refine_gradation
docs.text:
float · default 2.0

Gradation cap for the monotone sizing smoothing: adjacent sizings may differ by at most this factor (smoothing only lowers values).

docs.title: stuck_refine_force_split
docs.text:
bool · default true

When the max energy stalls, split each worst triangle's longest edge once, bypassing the split length gate, to unstick a sliver without changing the sizing field. Adds at most one split per worst triangle per stall -- but 'worst' means every triangle above the filter energy when stuck_refine_num_worst is 0, so on a mesh whose stop_energy sits close to the AMIPS2D floor of 2 this can force thousands of splits in one pass and blow up the element count. Bound stuck_refine_num_worst or turn this off in that regime.

docs.title: skip_good_regions
docs.text:
bool · default false

Only smooth vertices incident to a triangle whose energy is at least skip_good_regions_margin * stop_energy; skip smoothing already-good regions. OFF by default: smoothing is the only phase that improves quality without changing connectivity, and the premise that a vertex surrounded by good elements has nothing to gain is not reliable -- for surface vertices the move is driven by the envelope term rather than by element quality, which is why active_vertices() has to append every surface vertex unconditionally to keep the filter from freezing them outright. With the filter off that special case stops carrying the correctness of the pass. Measured in 2D on 122839 at stop_energy 20, filtering also cost more than it saved: 60 iterations ending at max energy 21.03 with it on, against convergence to 19.9998 in 54 iterations and less wall time (875s vs 947s) with it off. Note the threshold scales with stop_energy, so the filter skips far more at 100 than at 20.

docs.title: skip_good_regions_margin
docs.text:
float · default 0.9

A triangle is 'active' (worth smoothing around) when its energy is at least this fraction of stop_energy. The AMIPS2D energy of an equilateral triangle is 2, so the filter only skips anything once skip_good_regions_margin * stop_energy exceeds 2.

docs.title: coarsen_pass
docs.text:
bool · default false

Run a final coarsening pass after the optimization has converged. The ordinary collapse judges a candidate on the raw post-collapse geometry -- the worst moment in the operation's life, before smoothing has absorbed any of the damage -- so a collapse that would be fine once its neighbourhood relaxes is never taken, and the converged mesh keeps vertices it does not need. This pass takes the collapse optimistically, re-smooths coarsen_smooth_ring around the merged vertex, and keeps it only if the worst element in the region it touched is no worse than before; every element outside that region is untouched, so 'no worse locally' is exactly 'no worse globally'. Alternates with ordinary smoothing passes, as the main optimization does.

docs.title: coarsen_local_smoothing_passes
docs.text:
int · default 0

Smoothing sweeps over the ring, inside each candidate collapse, before judging it. 0 by default, which means the pass judges the collapse on its raw post-collapse geometry and never smooths inside the operation. At the level of a single candidate that matters -- the composite's reject rate rises from 25% to 39% without it -- but it does not cost coarsening, because the pass runs to a fixed point: a candidate the smoothing would have rescued is replaced by another the pass finds instead, and the relaxation the mesh actually needs comes from the global smoothing between rounds. What it costs is time. The smoothed ball averaged 98 vertices on tetwild's octocat, so at the old default of 2 sweeps one candidate ran ~200 nonlinear smoothing solves and the pass ran 1.4 million of them to accept 5173 collapses. Over seven tetwild models, dropping this to 0 (with coarsen_max_inner_passes 1) made the pass 9.7x to 31.9x faster for about 1 percentage point of cell reduction.

docs.title: coarsen_smooth_ring
docs.text:
int · default 1

Radius smoothed inside the collapse, and the radius the accept test measures over. The lock claims one more ring than this. With coarsen_local_smoothing_passes at 0 nothing is smoothed, so this only sets how wide a region the accept test compares; a wider region is a more permissive test (it admits untouched cells to both the before and after maxima, which is still sound) so ring 2 coarsens slightly more, but it also makes the pass lock 3 rings per operation where the ordinary collapse locks 2, which is the worst thing for its parallel scaling. 1 by default: on octocat that is 2.3x faster than ring 2 for 1.5 percentage points of cell reduction, and it puts the lock footprint back in line with every other pass.

docs.title: coarsen_global_smoothing_passes
docs.text:
int · default 1

Ordinary whole-mesh smoothing passes run between coarsening rounds. This is what makes a second round worth running at all -- see coarsen_max_rounds -- so setting it to 0 collapses the rounds to one.

docs.title: coarsen_max_rounds
docs.text:
int · default 2

Cap on the coarsen/smooth alternation; the pass also stops as soon as a round accepts no collapse.
